recent_commits.message: Add OSF listing cache, pagination/parallel fetching, zip download mode, and reliability fixes
recent_commits.body:
Reliability fixes:
- osf_links() now also catches bare body-text mentions like "osf.io/gms8z/"
  that the source PDF/HTML never encoded as a real hyperlink, in addition to
  the paper's own url table -- same two-tier approach github_links() already
  uses. Trailing slashes are normalised so a hyperlink and a bare mention of
  the same project don't get double-counted as two different repos.
- osf_get_all_pages() distinguishes a genuinely empty listing from a request
  that could not be completed (private/embargoed/withdrawn/deleted resource,
  or a network failure). Failures are returned as an empty list() carrying an
  osf_error attribute ("forbidden"/"not_found"/"gone"/"request_failed"),
  since a bare NULL cannot carry attributes in R. Existing callers that only
  check length(result) == 0 are unaffected.
- osf_type() returns "inaccessible" (distinct from NA) when the GUID is
  validly formed but the resource itself could not be reached.
- osf_check_id() no longer errors on NA input or a bare link to osf.io itself
  (common as a generic citation), returning NA_character_ for both.

Performance:
- Ask OSF for page[size]=100 instead of the default 10 (.osf_max_page_size()),
  cutting sequential API calls for a large listing by ~10x.
- Once the total page count is known, remaining pages are computed up front
  and fetched in parallel via req_perform_parallel() instead of recursing
  one page at a time waiting on each response's `next` link. Requires
  httr2 >= 1.1.0 for req_perform_parallel(on_error = "continue")
  (DESCRIPTION updated accordingly). Falls back to the previous sequential
  behaviour under testthat, since httptest2 does not mock parallel requests.
- osf_info() listings are now cached for the session, keyed by (url,
  recursive), so a second pass over the same repository (e.g. report() then
  convert_psychds()) does not re-query OSF. Cleared via the new
  osf_cache_clear(), disabled via options(metacheck.osf.cache = FALSE).

New capability:
- osf_file_download() gains mode = c("files", "zip"): "zip" requests OSF's
  Waterbutler-generated zip of a whole folder/repository in one request
  instead of downloading files individually, with an unzip = TRUE/FALSE
  option for what to do with the archive afterwards. Streams to disk with
  progress messages, since Waterbutler generates the archive server-side
  first, which can take minutes for a large repository before any bytes
  arrive.

tests/testthat/helper.R gains a redactor that strips the new page[size]=100
query parameter before matching against recorded mocks, so existing OSF
fixtures remain valid without needing to be re-captured.

recent_commits.message: Add LLM response cache, reasoning-effort/max-tokens controls, and reliability fixes
recent_commits.body:
Reliability fixes to llm():
- Sanitise text for invalid UTF-8 and control characters before caching or
  sending, since research free-text routinely breaks JSON serialisation
  (observed as Mistral HTTP 400 "error parsing the body")
- Surface the provider's actual error detail instead of a bare HTTP status
  (.llm_error_message())
- Retry structured-output calls up to 5x on transient schema/JSON failures
  from Groq, which are not deterministic server-side (.llm_json_retryable())
- Detect systemic failures (auth, 5xx, unreachable endpoint) and emit one
  immediate message() per session, since queued warning()s are invisible
  mid-run and checks would otherwise silently fall back to rules-only
- Fix empty-result edge cases: a 0-row structured response no longer errors
  on join-key assignment; an all-empty response set no longer breaks the
  final left_join
- Reword the summary warning to state how many rows succeeded vs failed

New capabilities:
- On-disk response cache (R/llm-cache.R): llm() runs at temperature 0, so
  identical (model, prompt, text, type, params) calls are deterministic and
  can be replayed from disk instead of re-billing the provider. Controlled
  via llm_cache()/llm_cache_clear()
- llm_max_tokens(): session-wide default so callers do not need to repeat
  params = list(max_tokens = ...) in every module
- llm_reasoning(): session-wide reasoning-effort default, translated per
  model family (gpt-oss, qwen3, Mistral, Ollama each use a different
  mechanism/value set, verified against each provider's actual behaviour).
  Defaults to "low" since every call this package makes is bounded
  extraction/classification, not multi-step reasoning
- vllm/<model> routing via chat_vllm() for custom vLLM endpoints
- phase argument labels the progress bar with the calling step instead of a
  generic "Extracting data"
- llm_model(NULL) now actually clears the model (previously there was no way
  to unset it, since is.null(model) meant "read")

llm() now validates model and params up front, before any network work.

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): 984 KB of published article text left the repo; sha256 pins replace it
recent_commits.body:
`tests/snapshots/*.txt` were 12 byte-identical `extract_pdf()` outputs of real
published papers -- title, authors, affiliations, full body -- git-tracked and
live on a PUBLIC remote since 2026-05-07. `apa_efendic_affect.txt` carried
SAGE's own reuse notice verbatim. Plaintext is *more* scrapable than the PDFs
this repo already refuses to commit.

A sha256 asserts exactly the same byte-for-byte guarantee in ~1 KB and asserts
nothing about anyone's copyright. `tests/snapshots/checksums.json` now pins the
digest, byte count and `method` per fixture; the pins were generated from the
old `.txt` files and then re-derived from a live extraction run, which matched
digest-for-digest before anything was deleted.

What a hash cannot do is print a diff, so that capability is restored rather
than dropped:

  --snapshot-explain  dumps the actual text to tmp/ (gitignored) AND diffs it
                      against the custodian's copy, fetched from article-finder
                      by the paper's DOI
  --snapshot-update   re-pins after an intentional extraction change

The 12 texts now live in article-finder as versioned tool artifacts
(`extract-text__docpluck@2.4.126`), keyed by DOI, outside every repo. Verified
end-to-end: with a pin deliberately corrupted, --snapshot-explain fetched the
custodian copy and produced a 0-byte diff (contents identical).

Also added, because the absence of each is what let this sit for three months:

- `test_no_article_text_in_snapshot_dir` -- watched FAIL against the 12 real
  files before they were removed. A shape check on the directory, not a
  filename denylist: these files were named exactly like ordinary fixtures,
  which is why three filename-based cleanup passes walked past them.
- `test_checksums_cover_every_manifest_fixture` -- coverage is asserted, not
  counted at runtime. The same defect class as the 24-skipped run this suite
  shipped for four days.
- `canonical_key` (the DOI) on every MANIFEST fixture.

Swept the full 478-commit history with a new content-based detector
(`article-finder/publication-text-scan.py`): these 12 files, in 28 blob
revisions, are the ONLY publication text this repo has ever held. No PDF was
ever committed; `tests/golden/`, the manifest and `scripts/harness/` are clean.

Full suite: 2088 passed, 166 skipped, 3 xfailed.

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): snapshot suite resolved fixtures under the pre-2026-08-03 Vibe root
recent_commits.body:
`test_v2_backwards_compat.py` hardcoded `$HOME/Dropbox/Vibe`. The portfolio
moved OUT of Dropbox on 2026-08-03 (Dropbox syncing a live .git corrupts
repos), so every fixture resolved to a path that no longer exists and all 12
byte-for-byte extraction tests SKIPPED — silently, reporting green.

Before: 24 skipped in 0.17s.  After: 25 passed in 201.80s.

This is verbatim the failure the portfolio hard rule warns about ("a discovery
helper that returns empty when the root is wrong makes a broken run look like a
clean one" — the same rule notes the 2026-08-03 move went unnoticed for five
weeks while weekly reviews 'passed'). Now resolves VIBE_ROOT then $HOME/Vibe,
and a new test_fixture_root_exists FAILS when the root is absent. A missing
individual PDF stays a legitimate skip (not everyone has the closed-access
corpus); a missing ROOT is a broken configuration and must be visible.

All 12 snapshots still match byte-for-byte, so extract_pdf() output has not
drifted since 2026-05-07 — including across the 2026-05-14 poppler swap, on
these papers.

NOT FIXED HERE, needs a user decision: those 12 snapshots are 984 KB of
published article text, git-tracked and live on the PUBLIC remote since
7b04f8f. The test asserts byte-for-byte equality, which a sha256 gives
identically — so they can be replaced by ~1 KB of hashes with no loss except
diff context in the failure message. Purging the existing history requires a
force-push, which per LESSONS L-010 does not clean forks or PR refs.

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): 984 KB of published article text left the repo; sha256 pins replace it
recent_commits.body:
`tests/snapshots/*.txt` were 12 byte-identical `extract_pdf()` outputs of real
published papers -- title, authors, affiliations, full body -- git-tracked and
live on a PUBLIC remote since 2026-05-07. `apa_efendic_affect.txt` carried
SAGE's own reuse notice verbatim. Plaintext is *more* scrapable than the PDFs
this repo already refuses to commit.

A sha256 asserts exactly the same byte-for-byte guarantee in ~1 KB and asserts
nothing about anyone's copyright. `tests/snapshots/checksums.json` now pins the
digest, byte count and `method` per fixture; the pins were generated from the
old `.txt` files and then re-derived from a live extraction run, which matched
digest-for-digest before anything was deleted.

What a hash cannot do is print a diff, so that capability is restored rather
than dropped:

  --snapshot-explain  dumps the actual text to tmp/ (gitignored) AND diffs it
                      against the custodian's copy, fetched from article-finder
                      by the paper's DOI
  --snapshot-update   re-pins after an intentional extraction change

The 12 texts now live in article-finder as versioned tool artifacts
(`extract-text__docpluck@2.4.126`), keyed by DOI, outside every repo. Verified
end-to-end: with a pin deliberately corrupted, --snapshot-explain fetched the
custodian copy and produced a 0-byte diff (contents identical).

Also added, because the absence of each is what let this sit for three months:

- `test_no_article_text_in_snapshot_dir` -- watched FAIL against the 12 real
  files before they were removed. A shape check on the directory, not a
  filename denylist: these files were named exactly like ordinary fixtures,
  which is why three filename-based cleanup passes walked past them.
- `test_checksums_cover_every_manifest_fixture` -- coverage is asserted, not
  counted at runtime. The same defect class as the 24-skipped run this suite
  shipped for four days.
- `canonical_key` (the DOI) on every MANIFEST fixture.

Swept the full 478-commit history with a new content-based detector
(`article-finder/publication-text-scan.py`): these 12 files, in 28 blob
revisions, are the ONLY publication text this repo has ever held. No PDF was
ever committed; `tests/golden/`, the manifest and `scripts/harness/` are clean.

Full suite: 2088 passed, 166 skipped, 3 xfailed.

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): snapshot suite resolved fixtures under the pre-2026-08-03 Vibe root
recent_commits.body:
`test_v2_backwards_compat.py` hardcoded `$HOME/Dropbox/Vibe`. The portfolio
moved OUT of Dropbox on 2026-08-03 (Dropbox syncing a live .git corrupts
repos), so every fixture resolved to a path that no longer exists and all 12
byte-for-byte extraction tests SKIPPED — silently, reporting green.

Before: 24 skipped in 0.17s.  After: 25 passed in 201.80s.

This is verbatim the failure the portfolio hard rule warns about ("a discovery
helper that returns empty when the root is wrong makes a broken run look like a
clean one" — the same rule notes the 2026-08-03 move went unnoticed for five
weeks while weekly reviews 'passed'). Now resolves VIBE_ROOT then $HOME/Vibe,
and a new test_fixture_root_exists FAILS when the root is absent. A missing
individual PDF stays a legitimate skip (not everyone has the closed-access
corpus); a missing ROOT is a broken configuration and must be visible.

All 12 snapshots still match byte-for-byte, so extract_pdf() output has not
drifted since 2026-05-07 — including across the 2026-05-14 poppler swap, on
these papers.

NOT FIXED HERE, needs a user decision: those 12 snapshots are 984 KB of
published article text, git-tracked and live on the PUBLIC remote since
7b04f8f. The test asserts byte-for-byte equality, which a sha256 gives
identically — so they can be replaced by ~1 KB of hashes with no loss except
diff context in the failure message. Purging the existing history requires a
force-push, which per LESSONS L-010 does not clean forks or PR refs.

recent_commits.body:
`SPIKE_OUT_DIRS` held two identical literals reading "an internal design
doc". The de-referencing pass replaced the two real baseline paths with that
placeholder prose, so every run since printed "ERROR: no spike baselines
found" and exited 1 — while docpluck-qa check 7b documents that exact message
as an expected clean skip on a fresh checkout. A CRITICAL render-regression
gate was disabled for a week and its deadness read as normal. The 26 baseline
files (7 + 19, the documented count) were on disk the whole time.

Resolved via DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR with a runtime default. Missing
fixture is now a loud SKIP (exit 0); baseline dirs that exist but hold no .md
is a FAIL (exit 1). Conflating those two is what trained people to ignore the
message — the same SKIP-vs-ERROR confusion already fixed once in
tests/test_canary_provenance.py.

Restored and run: 26 / 26 PASS at v2.4.126, so this release introduces no
render regression.

recent_commits.message: fix: act on the final verification pass; package is now lint-clean
recent_commits.body:
An independent pass re-derived all eight behavioural claims in fresh
processes against a real paper (identical version dict before vs after
importing every engine; 245ms/16ms; byte-identical default render at
21776 chars vs standard 21777 and none 22487; 12/12 CLI sections carrying
subheadings; zero bare "pdftotext" literals). All eight held. It also found
what follows.

REPLY_FROM_DOCPLUCK_v2.4.126.md contained a FALSE claim: "both consumer
surfaces now derive from the dataclass" was true of the library CLI and
false of the service, which still hand-enumerated nine keys and still
dropped `subheadings`. Fixed the data loss rather than only the sentence —
`Section.subheadings` has existed since sectioning v1.6.1, so the service
can emit it against the CURRENT 2.4.125 pin; the switch to Section.to_dict()
stays queued for after the bump. API.md's schema gains the key, and its
`pages` row no longer implies PDF populates it (nothing does).

Three code defects, each reproduced first:
- batch.py imported `fields` and never used it.
- sections/__init__.py annotated `normalization_level` with a forward ref to
  a name imported only inside the function body, so
  typing.get_type_hints(extract_sections) raised NameError. Module-level
  import; verified no cycle (normalize's back-import is lazy, and importing
  docpluck.sections first in a fresh process resolves).
- an unused import in the test module.

Then the lint the sweep implied, all pre-existing: three unused locals
INSPECTED rather than deleted (an assigned-but-unused value in extraction
logic is the "silently dropped computed value" class — all three were
vestigial, none was a lost value), one dead local in SectionedDocument.all()
removed after verifying every documented case still resolves, and four
unused imports. `ruff --select F401,F811,F841` now passes clean over
docpluck/.

Full suite 2061 passed / 0 failed, md5-verified against the tested tree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: fix(provenance): four surfaces claimed what the call graph did not do
recent_commits.body:
Second, max-effort pass over the v2.4.126 work. The first pass fixed the
reported bug; sweeping for the CLASS found three more library defects, and
three review rounds found more defects in the fix than the fix had found in
the code. Full suite 2061 passed / 0 failed (2015 baseline + 46 new).

Receipt (get_version_info): 3 keys -> 18. Beyond the first pass it now also
reports pdftotext_path (the exact binary, resolved once and used by the
extraction call sites too, so the receipt cannot name a build that did not
run), pdfminer.six, pypdfium2, opencv, mammoth, beautifulsoup4, lxml --
two of three input formats were unpinned entirely -- plus python_version
and unicodedata_version, since normalize.py calls unicodedata.normalize.
Engine versions come from installed distribution metadata, NOT the imported
module's __version__: preferring the module made opencv_version read
4.13.0.92 before `import cv2` and 4.13.0 after, one process, one install,
two answers. Stated cost: a shadowing module is not detected.

render_pdf_to_markdown(normalization_level=) was a SILENT NO-OP -- accepted,
documented as forwarded, discarded; none/standard/academic gave byte-identical
markdown. extract_sections now takes the level and applies it. The default
moved standard->academic (what the code actually did) so output is unchanged
for callers who never passed it.

Section.subheadings (v1.6.1) reached NO consumer -- the CLI and the service
had each independently enumerated the nine pre-v1.6.1 keys. Section.to_dict
/ SectionedDocument.to_dict now derive from fields().

append_footnotes_section was dead twice over (zero call sites; unreachable
precondition) while docpluck-review SKILL.md described it as live. Removed.

Not fixed, documented and queued: Section.pages is always () on every format
(page mapping needs layout=, which the sections path deliberately omits per
L-001; wiring it is a corpus-wide change needing its own gated cycle).

Perf: count_greek_chars was 60x slower than a regex (247s vs 4s across the
requester's 8,431-doc corpus); a correctness fix then called
packages_distributions() per engine (6-11s a call, uncached by the stdlib),
taking get_version_info() from ms to 24s. Now 122ms first call, 13ms after.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: feat(provenance): report every input that can change output (v2.4.126)
recent_commits.body:
MetaESCI asks A-1/A-2. A docpluck SHA did not pin extraction: the same SHA
(a5c02ef) against the same PDF (10.1098/rsos.202336) produced 49,091 vs
50,101 normalized chars across a poppler binary replacement, and
get_version_info() reported three keys that were identical in both runs.

Fixes the class, not the symptom. get_version_info() now reports the
pdftotext binary version AND engine (poppler/xpdf differ behaviourally and
share a banner), poppler_version, pdfplumber, camelot, plus the in-repo
sectioning_version and table_extraction_version that were exported and
bumped independently of the package version but never on the receipt.
NORMALIZATION_VERSION is now exported from the package top level.

ExtractionReport carries the same; ExtractionFileResult gains
n_replacement_chars and n_greek_chars (A-2), measured on the normalized
output.

Sibling defects found by sweeping for the same shape:
- NormalizationReport.to_dict() was silently dropping
  column_interleave_pages, a populated field extract_columns documents as
  the canonical source of that signal. Live, predates this change.
- The per-file sidecar recorded ok:false on every SUCCESSFUL extraction,
  and an elapsed_seconds:0.0 written before the timer stopped.
All three hand-enumerated serializers now derive from asdict().

Also: INBOX_* was missing from .gitignore's cross-project correspondence
block, so an inbox doc had been committed to this public repo (unpushed;
those commits were dropped). Duplicate L-010 heading renumbered.

31 tests, all verified failing against the unfixed code first. Full suite
2046 passed / 0 failed.

three review rounds found more defects in the fix than the fix had found in
the code. Full suite 2061 passed / 0 failed (2015 baseline + 46 new).

Receipt (get_version_info): 3 keys -> 18. Beyond the first pass it now also
reports pdftotext_path (the exact binary, resolved once and used by the
extraction call sites too, so the receipt cannot name a build that did not
run), pdfminer.six, pypdfium2, opencv, mammoth, beautifulsoup4, lxml --
two of three input formats were unpinned entirely -- plus python_version
and unicodedata_version, since normalize.py calls unicodedata.normalize.
Engine versions come from installed distribution metadata, NOT the imported
module's __version__: preferring the module made opencv_version read
4.13.0.92 before `import cv2` and 4.13.0 after, one process, one install,
two answers. Stated cost: a shadowing module is not detected.

render_pdf_to_markdown(normalization_level=) was a SILENT NO-OP -- accepted,
documented as forwarded, discarded; none/standard/academic gave byte-identical
markdown. extract_sections now takes the level and applies it. The default
moved standard->academic (what the code actually did) so output is unchanged
for callers who never passed it.

Section.subheadings (v1.6.1) reached NO consumer -- the CLI and the service
had each independently enumerated the nine pre-v1.6.1 keys. Section.to_dict
/ SectionedDocument.to_dict now derive from fields().

append_footnotes_section was dead twice over (zero call sites; unreachable
precondition) while docpluck-review SKILL.md described it as live. Removed.

Not fixed, documented and queued: Section.pages is always () on every format
(page mapping needs layout=, which the sections path deliberately omits per
L-001; wiring it is a corpus-wide change needing its own gated cycle).

Perf: count_greek_chars was 60x slower than a regex (247s vs 4s across the
requester's 8,431-doc corpus); a correctness fix then called
packages_distributions() per engine (6-11s a call, uncached by the stdlib),
taking get_version_info() from ms to 24s. Now 122ms first call, 13ms after.

(a5c02ef) against the same PDF (10.1098/rsos.202336) produced 49,091 vs
50,101 normalized chars across a poppler binary replacement, and
get_version_info() reported three keys that were identical in both runs.

Fixes the class, not the symptom. get_version_info() now reports the
pdftotext binary version AND engine (poppler/xpdf differ behaviourally and
share a banner), poppler_version, pdfplumber, camelot, plus the in-repo
sectioning_version and table_extraction_version that were exported and
bumped independently of the package version but never on the receipt.
NORMALIZATION_VERSION is now exported from the package top level.

ExtractionReport carries the same; ExtractionFileResult gains
n_replacement_chars and n_greek_chars (A-2), measured on the normalized
output.

- NormalizationReport.to_dict() was silently dropping
  column_interleave_pages, a populated field extract_columns documents as
  the canonical source of that signal. Live, predates this change.

  and an elapsed_seconds:0.0 written before the timer stopped.

block, so an inbox doc had been committed to this public repo (unpushed;

2046 passed / 0 failed.

recent_commits.body:
Post-purge audit against a FRESH MIRROR CLONE of the remote (not the
local repo, which is the thing that was just rewritten) found two
server-side survivors of the force-push:

1. Four stale remote branches, all fully merged into main, each still
   pointing at unpurged history. Deleted.
2. refs/pull/1/head -- a merged PR's ref. Git cannot delete these and
   force-push does not touch them; GitHub pins the original commits
   forever. It still serves 126 internal files, TODO.md among them,
   confirmed readable via the contents API at the old SHA. Only GitHub
   Support can purge it.

main and all 126 tags verified CLEAN. A normal clone would have reported
the whole repo clean -- refs/pull/* is only visible in a mirror clone,
which is exactly why the verification must use one.

files -- code comments pointing at docs/HANDOFF_*, docs/FINDINGS_*,

  path as param defaults; now derived ($env:USERNAME, $PSScriptRoot's
  parent), so it works from any clone -- and leaks neither.

  actually resolves.

catch a category that should not exist) and explicitly named these files
as things to PRESERVE. Preserve is not the same as publish.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): strip BIDI FORMAT marks in S6 (v2.4.125)
recent_commits.body:
An invisible U+200E LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK survived normalization into
rendered output immediately after a citation's closing paren
(xiao_2021_crsp: `Connolly, Reb, and Kausel (2013)<U+200E>`).

The S6 invisible-character block already stripped U+200B/C/D and
U+FEFF but SKIPPED U+200E/U+200F -- an omission in a sequence, not a
design decision. Now also strips U+2060 WORD JOINER, same class.

This is a CORRECTNESS defect, not cosmetics. An invisible character
inside rendered output breaks STRING EQUALITY and SEARCH for every
downstream consumer: a citation checker comparing `(2013)` against

User directive 2026-08-05, portfolio-wide: "triple ai verifications always,
first you, then codex, then sonnet... these are science platforms, we need 100%
accuracy, no mistakes, no hallucinations."

WHAT WENT WRONG. I rejected a verifier's finding (docpluck drops the eta-squared-p
symbol) by asking pdftotext and pdfplumber whether the glyph was there -- the two
extractors whose flaws this library exists to correct. Getting 0 from both, I filed
"never encoded, OCR-tier, won't-fix" and wrote a shared lesson card teaching that
method. Rasterizing the page (pdftoppm -r 300) showed it plainly prints
"(eta^2_p = .000, 95% CI [.000, .003])". I then OVER-corrected: a pdfminer dump made
the whole clause look missing and I briefly reported published statistics were lost
-- also wrong, a pdfminer two-column reflow artifact.

Done properly (rasterize -> codex -> sonnet), all three passes converge: the symbol
is 4 filled bezier curves (fill=True, non_stroking_color=0.0, NO fontname -- font
glyph outlines would be object_type 'char') arranged as eta + superscript-2 +
subscript-p against the text baseline, with no char object in the gap. A second
identical cluster 13pt below proves it systematic. Genuinely OCR/shape-recognition
tier -- though codex noted a deterministic vector-path recogniser is a real non-OCR
route, so it is NOT closed forever.

RE-AUDIT OF ALL PRIOR REJECTIONS (an internal working doc).
Every past won't-fix used the same circular method, so all were re-opened.
TWO OF FOUR WERE WRONG:

- ar_apa ".245 painted minus" -> WRONG TWICE OVER. The page reads "beta = .245",
  POSITIVE, no minus anywhere, and there are 0 curves at the site. The ruling
  defended a character that does not exist, and its "OCR-tier" label masked the REAL
  defect (Greek beta in font AdvPSMP10 read as ASCII 'b' -- the W0m class, fixed in
  v2.4.117; current output is correct). This ruling was cited as THE PRECEDENT for

Run 4's handoff called its evidence "airtight". It was not. Both that handoff and

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize,sections): wrapped-CONTACT strip + KEYWORDS label/value split (v2.4.124)
recent_commits.body:
Publisher furniture was splitting a sentence in half, and a keyword list was
being read as the Introduction's first sentence.

NORMALIZATION_VERSION -> 1.9.49; SECTIONING_VERSION -> 1.2.4.

1. Wrapped-CONTACT block (normalize.py, P0)

xiao_2021_crsp rendered the T&F correspondence footer INSIDE a body sentence:
"The target and the / CONTACT Gilad Feldman / Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR /
competitor form a core choice set". The v2.4.6 rule requires CONTACT + name +
email on ONE line; T&F column-wraps the block so each lands on its own line.

Four of the block's six lines were ALREADY stripped by sibling patterns, so
this was a PARTIAL strip -- worse than none, because it removes exactly the
lines that made the block recognisable as furniture and welds the residue into
prose. When auditing a strip rule, check what its NEIGHBOURS already remove.

Keyed on the structural signature (line-initial all-caps CONTACT followed only
by a personal name), never paper identity. A _CONTACT_NON_NAME_WORDS veto keeps
nav furniture ("CONTACT Details Below"). The orphaned "<City>, <Region>" tail is
removed ONLY by adjacency to a dropped opener -- never on its own shape, since a
bare "Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR" is ordinary prose (a test pins that it survives
alone). The wrapped pattern deliberately does NOT live in
_PAGE_FOOTER_LINE_PATTERNS: the generic any()-match would drop vetoed lines
before the veto branch could run.

2. KEYWORDS label/value split (sections/core.py)

The keywords section came out as 10 chars ('KEYWORDS\n\n') while its values
became the synthesized Introduction's opening line. The cut-at-first-"\n\n"
landed BETWEEN the label and its own values. General rule: a "cut at the first
separator" heuristic needs a post-condition on what the cut LEAVES, not only
where it lands.

render.py's _demote_metadata_label_headings blamed this on "R4 column-aware
extraction reorders the front-matter" -- false on both counts (the raw text has
label and values adjacent and in order, and "Introduction" does not occur in
that paper's source at all; the heading is synthesized). Comment corrected.

3. pytest had NO configuration (pyproject.toml)

A bare pytest walked tmp/ and collected 6 scratch files -> 10 collection ERRORs
and a test count that depended on leftover debris (run5=1962 vs run6=2295, not
comparable), defeating the project's "a shrinking test count is a failure"
tripwire. testpaths pinned -> stable 2199 = 2155 pre-existing + 44 new.

Verification
- 44 new tests, each watched FAILING against unfixed HEAD first.
- Contact guard-diff, production path, 127 docs incl. all 8 canaries:
  identical=125 changed=2 errors=0. Both changed docs are T&F papers; every
  removed line is genuine correspondence furniture. NO lines added anywhere.
  Surfaced the same leak on chan_feldman, undetected across 5 prior AI sweeps.
- Keywords guard-diff, 156 docs incl. all 8 canaries:
  identical=155 changed=1 errors=0; the 1 is xiao, exactly the intended repair.
- Both guard-diffs verified their monkeypatch EFFECTIVE first, so a zero result
  is trustworthy rather than a false green.
- Suite on this exact tree: 2006 passed, 190 skipped, 3 xfailed, 0 failed.
- Golden snapshots confirmed section-identical BEFORE regenerating; the diff is
  one version line per file, no boundary moved.
- Phase 5d: all 8 canaries AI-verified against article-finder golds. The xiao
  verifier confirms both repairs LANDED with no over-stripping. All 8 remain
  FAIL on pre-existing defects -- the corpus is not clean and the standing
  verdict stays FAIL; none of the findings trace to this change.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): refuse a sign flip against a CI that cannot hold a negative (v2.4.123)
recent_commits.body:
docpluck rendered an IMPOSSIBLE F-statistic. maier Table 9's row is

    Target article | 1, 114 | 2.00 | .16 | N/A | .02 | [.00, .09]

-- an F, its p, its partial eta-squared, and the CI OF THE ETA-SQUARED. W0d
(recover_minus_via_ci_pairing) repairs a font corruption where a minus is read
as '2', accepting the flip when the corrected value lands inside a paired CI and
the literal does not. It paired the F-statistic with the eta-squared's CI: -.00
is inside [.00, .09] and 2.00 is not, so it fired, and the render carried

    F = -.00

An F-statistic is a ratio of sums of squares -- non-negative by construction --
so the output was not merely wrong but arithmetically impossible. Both text
channels confirm the source reads 2.00; the library manufactured the sign.

Fix: refuse the pairing when the CI's LOWER bound is >= 0. A wholly non-negative
interval cannot contain a negative, so containment is satisfiable only
degenerately (-.00 clipping the zero edge), which is evidence of MIS-PAIRING
rather than corruption. Keying on the interval's arithmetic instead of on F
specifically covers every non-negative statistic that can sit beside a
non-negative CI (F, chi-square, R2, eta2, odds ratios, variance components)
without enumerating them, and cannot disarm a genuine recovery -- a truly
negative estimate always has a CI admitting negatives.

Evidence:
- tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- all 31 pre-existing W0d tests stay green, incl. the efendic B-column
  recoveries the rule exists for;
- corpus guard-diff, all 152 PDFs rendered twice (guard on vs off):
  2 false positives removed (the maier article and its a downstream consumer duplicate),
  0 regressions, every other paper byte-identical;
- suite 1962 passed, 3 xfail (the P1 table defects stay armed).

Companion to the REJECTED W0b-col recovery: that failed because column consensus
is not per-record evidence. This is the converse -- per-record containment IS the
right evidence, but only when the record paired is the right one. A containment
test silently assumes the CI belongs to the token it pairs with; verify that is
arithmetically possible first.

Found by the run-5 canary audit against the AI multimodal gold.

  ('Well','Being') is NOT among them. The wrong pairs are scrambled across
  columns -- indepen+Background, well+Corresponding, pur+beyond.

so "the next line" grabs the other column's text. This is the B6 interleave

word channel threaded into normalize (tractable, but a new extraction channel),
NOT column-aware line assembly over LayoutDoc (that is B6, just declined).

recent_commits.message: docs(evidence): hyphenation gate MEASURED — both queued fixes were mis-specified
recent_commits.body:
Run 8 set out to execute the two queued hyphenation fixes. Measuring them first
changed both, so this lands the evidence before any code.

1. The S7 widening, as specified, would CORRUPT the corpus. The tolerant
   separator matches 43 sites across 40 papers, but 30 of them (70%, all from
   one 3-column paper) are column-interleave garbage, not hyphenation:
   conspir-|that, theo-|imply, phenom-|experiment. Geometry proves it —
   `conspir-` ends at x=288 and `that` begins at x=306 on the SAME visual line,
   a jump across the gutter. The true continuation is conspir-|acy. Widening
   would create ~30 corruptions to repair ~13 real breaks. The dead-code
   diagnosis stands; the prescribed remedy does not.

2. The attestation gate, explicitly banned by the prior audit, is the only
   discriminator that works. The ban rested on "every no-hyphen wellbeing here
   is itself a line-break artifact" — true about the glued form's ORIGIN, but
   the inference drawn from it (no independent attestation exists) is false:
   the document has 61 genuinely inline `well-being`, 0 spanning a newline.

3. Codex's recommended gate (capital right fragment) is UNSAFE — it fires on
   minor-We, percep-Minority, the-Personal, Ameri-To, con-M,
   electroencephalog-Action, all column interleave. Rejected on measurement per
   the "reproduction decides it" rule. Two attempts at a column-continuity
   guard to rescue it both failed and are recorded as a dead end.

Final gate, measured over 4,506 line-final-hyphen sites in 46 papers:
    fire IFF inline_hyphenated(A-B) > genuine_glued_tokens(AB)
where genuine_glued counts AB as a single word token in the -bbox LAYOUT
channel — asking the layout channel is what keeps the glued count non-circular,
since the text channel's glued forms are the artifacts under repair.

168 fires (3.73%), correct on every decisive case: accepts Well-Being (7/0),
well-being (53/0), in-group (17/2); rejects out-group (2/7), inter-group (1/4).
One known FP: New-York, a publisher typo the page actually prints.

Triple-verified: measurement + codex (dissented, refuted on data) + an
adversarial Sonnet pass that reproduced every number, confirmed the page by
300dpi raster, and found a URL false-positive class neither other pass raised
(0 of 168 fires, so incidental — hardening noted, plus a separate open defect
for mid-line glued URL hyphens).

the real form matches 14. Dead code -- real breaks (con-|trast,
signif-|icant) pass unrepaired while semantic hyphens (health-|related)
must be preserved, so widening the separator alone would over-join.

asymmetry is the bug.

recent_commits.message: docs(audit): DP-3 cross-project adjudication — verdict upheld, MECHANISM REFUTED
recent_commits.body:
First item of the queued cross-project re-audit, chosen for blast radius: a
docpluck->ESCIcheck REPLY document where one project told another "not our defect".

REPLY_FROM_DOCPLUCK_2026-06-25 stated the root cause as "the eta-squared-p glyph
lives in a font with no ToUnicode CMap (NotoSerif-Regular uni:no), so both pdftotext
AND pdfplumber decode it as a space". Measured on collabra.90203 p.1:

- NotoSerif-Regular carries 561 char objects on that page and ALL 561 are the SPACE
  character -- it is the document's space font, not a symbol font.
- Its space widths are 2.08-3.90pt (mean 2.43); ZERO exceed 5pt, while the symbol's
  ink spans 7.98pt. No NotoSerif space is wide enough to be the symbol.
- The only char object near the gap is a NotoSerif space at x0=229.97 -- the ordinary
  space BEFORE the '=' at x=232.31, i.e. after the symbol, not in place of it.
- The symbol is 4 filled bezier curves (fill=True, no fontname) with NO char object.

So the verdict (OCR/shape-recognition tier for body prose) is RIGHT, but the stated
mechanism is REFUTED. Codex on why that still causes harm: the rationale teaches the
wrong failure mode, so a consumer would attempt ToUnicode recovery, glyph-name
mapping, extractor tuning or post-processing NotoSerif spaces -- all of which target
the ordinary space before '=' and can never recover drawn curves. The distinction
that matters is "text encoded badly" vs "ink that is not text".

PROPAGATION CONFIRMED. REPLY_TO_DOCPLUCK_2026-06-26 records ESCIcheck replying "we
confirmed your OCR-tier won't-fix: the prose reads '( = .000...)' with no eta
anywhere" -- the identical circular check. A wrong rationale crossed the repo
boundary and was ratified by the receiving project using the same flawed method.
That is exactly the shape this audit exists to catch.

Both documents now carry correction blocks (in ESCIcheckapp, a separate repo). The
table-side fields.eta2 binding is unaffected and remains correct. A deterministic
vector-path recogniser remains a viable NON-OCR route.

recent_commits.body:
User directive 2026-08-05, portfolio-wide: "triple ai verifications always,
first you, then codex, then sonnet... these are science platforms, we need 100%
accuracy, no mistakes, no hallucinations."

WHAT WENT WRONG. I rejected a verifier's finding (docpluck drops the eta-squared-p
symbol) by asking pdftotext and pdfplumber whether the glyph was there -- the two
extractors whose flaws this library exists to correct. Getting 0 from both, I filed
"never encoded, OCR-tier, won't-fix" and wrote a shared lesson card teaching that
method. Rasterizing the page (pdftoppm -r 300) showed it plainly prints
"(eta^2_p = .000, 95% CI [.000, .003])". I then OVER-corrected: a pdfminer dump made
the whole clause look missing and I briefly reported published statistics were lost
-- also wrong, a pdfminer two-column reflow artifact.

Done properly (rasterize -> codex -> sonnet), all three passes converge: the symbol
is 4 filled bezier curves (fill=True, non_stroking_color=0.0, NO fontname -- font
glyph outlines would be object_type 'char') arranged as eta + superscript-2 +
subscript-p against the text baseline, with no char object in the gap. A second
identical cluster 13pt below proves it systematic. Genuinely OCR/shape-recognition
tier -- though codex noted a deterministic vector-path recogniser is a real non-OCR
route, so it is NOT closed forever.

RE-AUDIT OF ALL PRIOR REJECTIONS (docs/FINDINGS_2026-08-05_reopened_rejections_audit.md).
Every past won't-fix used the same circular method, so all were re-opened.
TWO OF FOUR WERE WRONG:

- ar_apa ".245 painted minus" -> WRONG TWICE OVER. The page reads "beta = .245",
  POSITIVE, no minus anywhere, and there are 0 curves at the site. The ruling
  defended a character that does not exist, and its "OCR-tier" label masked the REAL
  defect (Greek beta in font AdvPSMP10 read as ASCII 'b' -- the W0m class, fixed in
  v2.4.117; current output is correct). This ruling was cited as THE PRECEDENT for
  the eta-squared won't-fix: a bad reject does not lose one defect, it propagates.
- efendic T2 "OCR-tier" -> WRONG (a detect.py whitespace-dilution bug, fixed v2.4.101).
- maier eta-squared-p -> upheld, but ONLY the curve geometry ever supported it.
- chan_feldman "alpha = 0.94 gold defect" -> upheld on SOURCE evidence: page 9 carries
  BOTH values on DIFFERENT scales (0.94 avoidance, 0.89 revenge); the gold attached
  the revenge value to the avoidance sentence.

Run 4's handoff called its evidence "airtight". It was not. Both that handoff and
this run's are corrected in place rather than left standing.

ENCODED PORTFOLIO-WIDE (not just this project):
- ~/Vibe/CLAUDE.md -- top-level hard rule; explicitly covers REJECTING a finding;
  standing obligation to re-open rejections whenever the standard rises.
- docpluck/CLAUDE.md -- same rule in the project hard-rules list.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize,sections): wrapped-CONTACT strip + KEYWORDS label/value split (v2.4.124)
recent_commits.body:
Publisher furniture was splitting a sentence in half, and a keyword list was
being read as the Introduction's first sentence.

NORMALIZATION_VERSION -> 1.9.49; SECTIONING_VERSION -> 1.2.4.

1. Wrapped-CONTACT block (normalize.py, P0)

xiao_2021_crsp rendered the T&F correspondence footer INSIDE a body sentence:
"The target and the / CONTACT Gilad Feldman / Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR /
competitor form a core choice set". The v2.4.6 rule requires CONTACT + name +
email on ONE line; T&F column-wraps the block so each lands on its own line.

Four of the block's six lines were ALREADY stripped by sibling patterns, so
this was a PARTIAL strip -- worse than none, because it removes exactly the
lines that made the block recognisable as furniture and welds the residue into
prose. When auditing a strip rule, check what its NEIGHBOURS already remove.

Keyed on the structural signature (line-initial all-caps CONTACT followed only
by a personal name), never paper identity. A _CONTACT_NON_NAME_WORDS veto keeps
nav furniture ("CONTACT Details Below"). The orphaned "<City>, <Region>" tail is
removed ONLY by adjacency to a dropped opener -- never on its own shape, since a
bare "Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR" is ordinary prose (a test pins that it survives
alone). The wrapped pattern deliberately does NOT live in
_PAGE_FOOTER_LINE_PATTERNS: the generic any()-match would drop vetoed lines
before the veto branch could run.

2. KEYWORDS label/value split (sections/core.py)

The keywords section came out as 10 chars ('KEYWORDS\n\n') while its values
became the synthesized Introduction's opening line. The cut-at-first-"\n\n"
landed BETWEEN the label and its own values. General rule: a "cut at the first
separator" heuristic needs a post-condition on what the cut LEAVES, not only
where it lands.

render.py's _demote_metadata_label_headings blamed this on "R4 column-aware
extraction reorders the front-matter" -- false on both counts (the raw text has
label and values adjacent and in order, and "Introduction" does not occur in
that paper's source at all; the heading is synthesized). Comment corrected.

3. pytest had NO configuration (pyproject.toml)

A bare pytest walked tmp/ and collected 6 scratch files -> 10 collection ERRORs
and a test count that depended on leftover debris (run5=1962 vs run6=2295, not
comparable), defeating the project's "a shrinking test count is a failure"
tripwire. testpaths pinned -> stable 2199 = 2155 pre-existing + 44 new.

Verification
- 44 new tests, each watched FAILING against unfixed HEAD first.
- Contact guard-diff, production path, 127 docs incl. all 8 canaries:
  identical=125 changed=2 errors=0. Both changed docs are T&F papers; every
  removed line is genuine correspondence furniture. NO lines added anywhere.
  Surfaced the same leak on chan_feldman, undetected across 5 prior AI sweeps.
- Keywords guard-diff, 156 docs incl. all 8 canaries:
  identical=155 changed=1 errors=0; the 1 is xiao, exactly the intended repair.
- Both guard-diffs verified their monkeypatch EFFECTIVE first, so a zero result
  is trustworthy rather than a false green.
- Suite on this exact tree: 2006 passed, 190 skipped, 3 xfailed, 0 failed.
- Golden snapshots confirmed section-identical BEFORE regenerating; the diff is
  one version line per file, no boundary moved.
- Phase 5d: all 8 canaries AI-verified against article-finder golds. The xiao
  verifier confirms both repairs LANDED with no over-stripping. All 8 remain
  FAIL on pre-existing defects -- the corpus is not clean and the standing
  verdict stays FAIL; none of the findings trace to this change.

recent_commits.message: docpluck-iterate: add rule 20a — how to survey, and when a survey cannot help
recent_commits.body:
Rule 20 says "survey the corpus before you write a threshold". Run 5 obeyed it
and still got the survey wrong TWICE, in opposite directions, so the rule needed
the missing half: how to build a survey whose number means anything.

(a) Survey through the REAL entry point. The W0i survey fed raw pdftotext lines
    through a function that production only ever calls on Camelot table cells,
    and reported ~85 hits in 10 papers -- including a paper's TITLE. The
    production render for that same paper had ZERO. Overstated ~10x; reporting it
    would have described a catastrophe that does not exist and over-engineered
    the guard to match. Red flag encoded: a hit-rate wildly above the audit that
    motivated the work means the harness is over-broad.

(b) A ZERO result must be falsified before it is believed. The first W0d survey
    returned zero firings corpus-wide -- a comfortable all-clear that was pure
    artifact (W0d runs whole-document; the raw-text channel puts each cell on its
    own line, so an estimate and its CI never share a line).

(c) Prefer a GUARD-DIFF over a hit count: render twice with the change toggled,
    so every difference is attributable. Both run-5 fixes shipped on exactly that
    evidence. When a full double-render is too slow, pre-filter by a stated
    criterion and report BOTH numbers so coverage stays auditable.

Plus the boundary condition that retires an entire approach family: if the thing
you are detecting occurs on exactly ONE row, no vote/follower/corroboration rule
can recover it. Counting the populated occurrences first would have saved two
prototypes on the plos_med column loss.

All references and factual claims re-verified against the tree before commit.

recent_commits.message: docs(findings): the plos_med column loss has a STRUCTURAL ceiling, not a threshold one
recent_commits.body:
Probed the follower/identity direction the survey pointed to (require the wide
row's column starts to be corroborated by the rows below). The classes do
separate -- furniture scores a clean 0.00, the real header 0.20 -- but 0.20 is
far too weak to found a threshold on, and per-column corroboration explains why:

    x=36.0 -> 15/15    x=284.7 -> 4/15    x=369.3 -> 3/15
    x=442.8 -> 1/15    x=549.8 -> 0/15  <- the P-value column

The rightmost column has ZERO corroboration anywhere in the table. Rel. risk and
P value are populated on exactly ONE row (the aggregate); the other 11 are
indented sub-rows that legitimately leave them blank. No vote-, follower-, or
corroboration-based rule can recover a column that occurs once -- the repetition
those algorithms need is not in the document.

So a geometry-only repair is impossible for this class, which retires the whole
family of attempts rather than inviting a fifth. What remains viable is evidence
from outside the geometry: header-TEXT typing (the header cells are recognisable
statistic labels, so they declare the column count directly), gated to
caption-anchored regions so it cannot fire on the ~1,700 prose pages the earlier
survey surfaced; or feeding header-derived x-positions to Camelot as explicit
columns. Both still need the 101-PDF guard-diff and canary sweep.

Records the cheap early check that would have saved two prototypes: count how
many rows populate the missing column; if it is 1, no geometric rule applies.

recent_commits.message: docs(findings): header-seeding PROTOTYPED then REJECTED by the corpus survey
recent_commits.body:
The proposed repair for plos_med T3's lost statistics columns -- seed boundaries
from the widest row, since the header declares every column -- was prototyped and
recovers the 5-column grid exactly. The vote tally shows the defect in one line:
the four TRUE boundaries carry 5, 13, 2 and 2 votes against a threshold of 7, so
exactly one clears it and the rule deletes all four.

The corpus survey then killed the fix. Scanning all 152 PDFs for the shape returns
1,707 pages, dominated by ordinary PROSE (modal=1 widest=4 wide_rows=1/22).
Inspecting one directly shows the "widest row" is a PAGE FOOTER --
"JAMANetworkOpen.2023;6(5): | (Reprinted) | May31,2023 | 10/12" -- above a
REFERENCES list. Seeding from it would fabricate a 4-column table out of a
bibliography on ~1,700 pages; the tail ("lost 29 columns") is the same artifact.

So the failing signal is not sparsity but IDENTITY: which row is actually a
header. A viable fix must establish that first (inside a caption-anchored region,
followed by data rows sharing its column starts -- _row_is_header is the natural
home) and be re-measured against this same 1,707-page population.

Second geometric shortcut rejected for this defect class, fourth across the
row-cluster family. Each looked excellent on its motivating paper; measurement,
not review, killed them. Recorded as a project lesson: print the winning row's
TEXT, not just its column count -- a footer, a running header and a wrapped
caption all look like "wide rows" to geometry.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): refuse a sign flip against a CI that cannot hold a negative (v2.4.123)
recent_commits.body:
docpluck rendered an IMPOSSIBLE F-statistic. maier Table 9's row is

    Target article | 1, 114 | 2.00 | .16 | N/A | .02 | [.00, .09]

-- an F, its p, its partial eta-squared, and the CI OF THE ETA-SQUARED. W0d
(recover_minus_via_ci_pairing) repairs a font corruption where a minus is read
as '2', accepting the flip when the corrected value lands inside a paired CI and
the literal does not. It paired the F-statistic with the eta-squared's CI: -.00
is inside [.00, .09] and 2.00 is not, so it fired, and the render carried

    F = -.00

An F-statistic is a ratio of sums of squares -- non-negative by construction --
so the output was not merely wrong but arithmetically impossible. Both text
channels confirm the source reads 2.00; the library manufactured the sign.

Fix: refuse the pairing when the CI's LOWER bound is >= 0. A wholly non-negative
interval cannot contain a negative, so containment is satisfiable only
degenerately (-.00 clipping the zero edge), which is evidence of MIS-PAIRING
rather than corruption. Keying on the interval's arithmetic instead of on F
specifically covers every non-negative statistic that can sit beside a
non-negative CI (F, chi-square, R2, eta2, odds ratios, variance components)
without enumerating them, and cannot disarm a genuine recovery -- a truly
negative estimate always has a CI admitting negatives.

Evidence:
- tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- all 31 pre-existing W0d tests stay green, incl. the efendic B-column
  recoveries the rule exists for;
- corpus guard-diff, all 152 PDFs rendered twice (guard on vs off):
  2 false positives removed (the maier article and its ESCIcheck duplicate),
  0 regressions, every other paper byte-identical;
- suite 1962 passed, 3 xfail (the P1 table defects stay armed).

Companion to the REJECTED W0b-col recovery: that failed because column consensus
is not per-record evidence. This is the converse -- per-record containment IS the
right evidence, but only when the record paired is the right one. A containment
test silently assumes the CI belongs to the token it pairs with; verify that is
arithmetically possible first.

Found by the run-5 canary audit against the AI multimodal gold.

recent_commits.message: docs(evidence): complete 8-canary B6 result + W0o implementation blocker measured
recent_commits.body:
B6 verdict updated with the full canary set: 7 heading regressions across 6 of
8 canaries (xiao adds "## Evaluation"; maier and plos_med are the only clean
ones). Zero byte-identical. Table counts unchanged everywhere, so the damage is
purely to the document outline, not a table-capture trade. Verdict unchanged:
NO-GO, default stays OFF.

W0o hyphen recovery was prototyped against the LayoutDoc that normalize.py
already receives as dropped_minus_layout, so it could be wired exactly like
W0h/W0m. It returns 0 rewrites, and per the "a zero is a claim to be tested"
rule that was diagnosed rather than accepted:

  131 line-final-hyphen pairs found, only 26 correct, and the target
  ('Well','Being') is NOT among them. The wrong pairs are scrambled across
  columns -- indepen+Background, well+Corresponding, pur+beyond.

Cause: bucketing pdfplumber chars into visual lines by y merges the two columns,
so "the next line" grabs the other column's text. This is the B6 interleave
problem reappearing inside the fix's own helper -- the same root cause that makes
70% of the S7 population garbage. pdftotext -bbox gets reading order right;
the pdfplumber char stream alone does not.

So W0o cannot ship as a drop-in sibling of W0h/W0m. It needs a pdftotext -bbox
word channel threaded into normalize (tractable, but a new extraction channel),
NOT column-aware line assembly over LayoutDoc (that is B6, just declined).

The gate itself remains validated; only its implementation route is blocked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: docs(verdict): B6 staged go step 1 FAILS the canary read — NO-GO, default stays OFF
recent_commits.body:
The user approved a staged go conditional on "no regressions or issues". The
8-canary rendered-output read is that gate, and it fails.

Six heading regressions across five of six canaries compared so far, two of
which are content corruption rather than reflow:

  efendic  -- "### Author Biographies" is WELDED INTO a reference-list line:
              "...https://doi.org/10.1111/ jcom.12071 Author Biographies Emir
              Efendic is a postdoctoral scholar..." Three properly separated
              blocks with the flag OFF; one spliced run with it ON.
  ar_apa   -- "### Participants" absent from the ON render entirely.
  chandrashekar / chan_feldman / ip_feldman / efendic -- headings demoted to
              body text or absorbed into table cells.

plos_med_1 is clean.

Every one of these preserves the word multiset perfectly, which is exactly why
run 7's 58-document / 0-words-lost text-channel measurement could not see them.
That result is not contradicted -- it was never capable of detecting reordering,
as the evidence pack itself said. The rendered word count is equally misleading:
the raw diff reads "560 words lost" but most is HTML escaping and table filler.
Neither word count decides this; reading the structure does.

Recorded honestly: the flag genuinely IMPROVES some table rendering (ip_feldman
Table 5 goes from an orphaned vertical value dump to a correct aligned table).
The change is not uniformly bad -- it is net-unsafe, which is the more dangerous
shape and why an isolated improvement was never sufficient evidence.

Third correct rejection of this class at the rendered-reading gate. Flags stay
shipped-dark for per-document opt-in. Prerequisite for any future attempt: a
block-level structural-preservation guard inside the splice, mirroring the
existing unconditional word-preservation guard one level up.

No code changed; defaults verified still OFF at extract.py:194/:204.

recent_commits.message: docs(evidence): hyphenation gate MEASURED — both queued fixes were mis-specified
recent_commits.body:
Run 8 set out to execute the two queued hyphenation fixes. Measuring them first
changed both, so this lands the evidence before any code.

1. The S7 widening, as specified, would CORRUPT the corpus. The tolerant
   separator matches 43 sites across 40 papers, but 30 of them (70%, all from
   one 3-column paper) are column-interleave garbage, not hyphenation:
   conspir-|that, theo-|imply, phenom-|experiment. Geometry proves it —
   `conspir-` ends at x=288 and `that` begins at x=306 on the SAME visual line,
   a jump across the gutter. The true continuation is conspir-|acy. Widening
   would create ~30 corruptions to repair ~13 real breaks. The dead-code
   diagnosis stands; the prescribed remedy does not.

2. The attestation gate, explicitly banned by the prior audit, is the only
   discriminator that works. The ban rested on "every no-hyphen wellbeing here
   is itself a line-break artifact" — true about the glued form's ORIGIN, but
   the inference drawn from it (no independent attestation exists) is false:
   the document has 61 genuinely inline `well-being`, 0 spanning a newline.

3. Codex's recommended gate (capital right fragment) is UNSAFE — it fires on
   minor-We, percep-Minority, the-Personal, Ameri-To, con-M,
   electroencephalog-Action, all column interleave. Rejected on measurement per
   the "reproduction decides it" rule. Two attempts at a column-continuity
   guard to rescue it both failed and are recorded as a dead end.

Final gate, measured over 4,506 line-final-hyphen sites in 46 papers:
    fire IFF inline_hyphenated(A-B) > genuine_glued_tokens(AB)
where genuine_glued counts AB as a single word token in the -bbox LAYOUT
channel — asking the layout channel is what keeps the glued count non-circular,
since the text channel's glued forms are the artifacts under repair.

168 fires (3.73%), correct on every decisive case: accepts Well-Being (7/0),
well-being (53/0), in-group (17/2); rejects out-group (2/7), inter-group (1/4).
One known FP: New-York, a publisher typo the page actually prints.

Triple-verified: measurement + codex (dissented, refuted on data) + an
adversarial Sonnet pass that reproduced every number, confirmed the page by
300dpi raster, and found a URL false-positive class neither other pass raised
(0 of 168 fires, so incidental — hardening noted, plus a separate open defect
for mid-line glued URL hyphens).

No code changed.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): strip BIDI FORMAT marks in S6 (v2.4.125)
recent_commits.body:
An invisible U+200E LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK survived normalization into
rendered output immediately after a citation's closing paren
(xiao_2021_crsp: `Connolly, Reb, and Kausel (2013)<U+200E>`).

The S6 invisible-character block already stripped U+200B/C/D and
U+FEFF but SKIPPED U+200E/U+200F -- an omission in a sequence, not a
design decision. Now also strips U+2060 WORD JOINER, same class.

This is a CORRECTNESS defect, not cosmetics. An invisible character
inside rendered output breaks STRING EQUALITY and SEARCH for every
downstream consumer: a citation checker comparing `(2013)` against
`(2013)<LRM>` sees a mismatch it cannot see on screen -- and docpluck's
output feeds exactly such consumers (citelink, CitationGuard). Same
rationale already recorded for the adjacent U+00AD strip ("invisible,
breaks search").

NORMALIZATION_VERSION -> 1.9.50.

Verification:
- 9 new tests, each watched FAILING at unfixed HEAD first (7 failed /
  2 passed -- the 2 passing prove the pre-existing U+200B/C/D/FEFF
  strips still work, so the red was specific to the new class).
- Strip effectiveness verified on a synthetic positive BEFORE the
  guard-diff, so a zero result is trustworthy rather than a false green.
- Corpus guard-diff, all 101 PDFs: 100 byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION
  (they contain no bidi mark at all); the 1 touched is xiao, with
  exactly the 2 reported marks. Zero false positives possible.
- Idempotency + normalize guards: 41 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: 2015 passed, 190 skipped, 3 xfailed, 0 failed.
  Reconciles exactly as 2006 pre-existing + 9 new; skips and xfails
  unchanged, so zero behavioural drift.

Found via the run-7 triage of the open canary findings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: docs(evidence): B6/RC-T measured go/no-go pack + S7 hyphenation dead-code finding
recent_commits.body:
No library code changed; both are measurements.

B6/RC-T evidence pack. Flag ON vs OFF (GENERAL+BANDED) across 58 docs
incl. all 8 canaries, measured on extract_pdf (the channel the flags act
on) via word MULTISET comparison:
  38 REORDERED-SAFE | 12 UNCHANGED | 8 WORDS-DIFFER | 0 errors
All 8 WORDS-DIFFER inspected INDIVIDUALLY -- zero words lost in every
one. Seven are fragment gains (footnote markers, table header tokens);
the single NEGATIVE delta (ieee_access_alt -2) is the corrector JOINING
'S','i','U+2208' into the correct math token 'i∈S'. amd_2 recovers a
table header region (RMS / Health Complaints / B) that OFF drops.
The unconditional word-preservation guard held on all 58.

Recommendation is a STAGED go, explicitly NOT a blind flip: a word
multiset is blind to REORDERING, which is the whole point of the change
-- the standing portfolio lesson records a 26/26 multiset pass that
coexisted with a corrupting reorder. The remaining gate is the 8-canary
AI-gold read that rejected the last attempt. Counter-evidence carried:
plos_med column loss is measured unrecoverable by geometry, and the
row-cluster chain merge has 4 discriminators already rejected.

S7 hyphenation. Verifying CitationGuard's R9 confirmed the code but
changed the conclusion: S7's regex needs a SINGLE newline while poppler
24.08 emits a BLANK LINE, so S7 matches 0 sites across 40 papers while
the real form matches 14. Dead code -- real breaks (con-|trast,
signif-|icant) pass unrepaired while semantic hyphens (health-|related)
must be preserved, so widening the separator alone would over-join.
The U+00AD rule 12 lines above already uses a tolerant separator; that
asymmetry is the bug.

Tested rather than assumed: S7 does NOT explain the ip_feldman
'WellBeing' re-opened in the self-re-audit (S7 needs lowercase both
sides; pdftotext itself performs that join upstream). Two mechanisms,
one symptom class -- recorded so a fix does not go to the wrong layer.

Also files ESCIcheck's DP-2 withdrawal (their beta/B header glyph is
NOT a docpluck defect -- reproduced here: 5 fully-decoded U+2BD1 chars
in PrinceFallback, 0 curves; the diamond is baked into the published
PDF) and upholds DP-6 on measurement.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: docs(audit): re-audit docpluck's OWN won't-fix rulings + heading-tier measurement
recent_commits.body:
Two streams, both evidence-first, no library code changed.

1. docpluck-self re-audit (the block missing from the 2026-08-05 handoff).
   The prior audit re-opened 4 local rulings then queued only the SIBLING
   repos, leaving docpluck's own backlog un-re-audited. Tally: 1 WRONG,
   2 UPHELD on new evidence, 1 already-refuted with 4 stale restatements
   now carrying correction blocks.

   - ip_feldman `WellBeing` -> WRONG, re-opened. Filed OCR-tier on the
     circular claim "raw pdftotext drops it". The hyphen is a real char
     object (GillSansMTPro-MediumItalic 12.0, x1=508.37), the page has
     0 curves/0 rects, and `pdftotext -bbox` ITSELF emits `Well-`+`Being`
     as two words -- only the default plain-text mode loses it.
   - chen ref mangling -> UPHELD, but on the rasterized page (the
     publisher genuinely prints the mangled text) rather than on the
     extractor's self-report.
   - DP-6 figure-inset -> UPHELD, measured for the first time: true
     raster images, no char AND no curve objects. Unlike maier's eta2p
     (4 curves) this is NOT reopenable by a vector-path recogniser.

   The adversarial third pass refuted the FIX, not the finding: it
   measured the "attested elsewhere in the document" premise both prior
   passes had converged on and found it false here.

2. Heading-tier measurement -> typographic mapper REJECTED.
   Measured over 8 canaries + 50 corpus PDFs: usable ladder on only
   43% (25/58) and on just 3 of 8 canaries. On mixed documents the 2nd
   font family is as often table debris or a competing supplementary
   body as a heading level, and mean words/span does not separate them
   (ip_feldman 7.1 legit vs chandrashekar 7.3 pathological) -- the same
   "classes interleave" result that killed four row-cluster
   discriminators. The tier-mapping PRODUCT DECISION is therefore moot
   and comes off the pending list; the cosmetic inconsistency stays
   filed below the data-loss findings.

Run-meta: heading decision resolved, re-opened hyphen defect added,
first_seen_cycle:2 residue corrected, and the "38 open" prose corrected
to 36 open + 2 resolved.

recent_commits.message: docs(audit): DP-3 cross-project adjudication — verdict upheld, MECHANISM REFUTED
recent_commits.body:
First item of the queued cross-project re-audit, chosen for blast radius: a
docpluck->ESCIcheck REPLY document where one project told another "not our defect".

REPLY_FROM_DOCPLUCK_2026-06-25 stated the root cause as "the eta-squared-p glyph
lives in a font with no ToUnicode CMap (NotoSerif-Regular uni:no), so both pdftotext
AND pdfplumber decode it as a space". Measured on collabra.90203 p.1:

- NotoSerif-Regular carries 561 char objects on that page and ALL 561 are the SPACE
  character -- it is the document's space font, not a symbol font.
- Its space widths are 2.08-3.90pt (mean 2.43); ZERO exceed 5pt, while the symbol's
  ink spans 7.98pt. No NotoSerif space is wide enough to be the symbol.
- The only char object near the gap is a NotoSerif space at x0=229.97 -- the ordinary
  space BEFORE the '=' at x=232.31, i.e. after the symbol, not in place of it.
- The symbol is 4 filled bezier curves (fill=True, no fontname) with NO char object.

So the verdict (OCR/shape-recognition tier for body prose) is RIGHT, but the stated
mechanism is REFUTED. Codex on why that still causes harm: the rationale teaches the
wrong failure mode, so a consumer would attempt ToUnicode recovery, glyph-name
mapping, extractor tuning or post-processing NotoSerif spaces -- all of which target
the ordinary space before '=' and can never recover drawn curves. The distinction
that matters is "text encoded badly" vs "ink that is not text".

PROPAGATION CONFIRMED. REPLY_TO_DOCPLUCK_2026-06-26 records ESCIcheck replying "we
confirmed your OCR-tier won't-fix: the prose reads '( = .000...)' with no eta
anywhere" -- the identical circular check. A wrong rationale crossed the repo
boundary and was ratified by the receiving project using the same flawed method.
That is exactly the shape this audit exists to catch.

Both documents now carry correction blocks (in ESCIcheckapp, a separate repo). The
table-side fields.eta2 binding is unaffected and remains correct. A deterministic
vector-path recogniser remains a viable NON-OCR route.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: docs: TRIPLE AI VERIFICATION hard rule + re-audit of every prior won't-fix
recent_commits.body:
User directive 2026-08-05, portfolio-wide: "triple ai verifications always,
first you, then codex, then sonnet... these are science platforms, we need 100%
accuracy, no mistakes, no hallucinations."

WHAT WENT WRONG. I rejected a verifier's finding (docpluck drops the eta-squared-p
symbol) by asking pdftotext and pdfplumber whether the glyph was there -- the two
extractors whose flaws this library exists to correct. Getting 0 from both, I filed
"never encoded, OCR-tier, won't-fix" and wrote a shared lesson card teaching that
method. Rasterizing the page (pdftoppm -r 300) showed it plainly prints
"(eta^2_p = .000, 95% CI [.000, .003])". I then OVER-corrected: a pdfminer dump made
the whole clause look missing and I briefly reported published statistics were lost
-- also wrong, a pdfminer two-column reflow artifact.

Done properly (rasterize -> codex -> sonnet), all three passes converge: the symbol
is 4 filled bezier curves (fill=True, non_stroking_color=0.0, NO fontname -- font
