recent_commits.message: fix(normalize,sections): wrapped-CONTACT strip + KEYWORDS label/value split (v2.4.124)
recent_commits.body:
Publisher furniture was splitting a sentence in half, and a keyword list was
being read as the Introduction's first sentence.

NORMALIZATION_VERSION -> 1.9.49; SECTIONING_VERSION -> 1.2.4.

1. Wrapped-CONTACT block (normalize.py, P0)

xiao_2021_crsp rendered the T&F correspondence footer INSIDE a body sentence:
"The target and the / CONTACT Gilad Feldman / Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR /
competitor form a core choice set". The v2.4.6 rule requires CONTACT + name +
email on ONE line; T&F column-wraps the block so each lands on its own line.

Four of the block's six lines were ALREADY stripped by sibling patterns, so
this was a PARTIAL strip -- worse than none, because it removes exactly the
lines that made the block recognisable as furniture and welds the residue into
prose. When auditing a strip rule, check what its NEIGHBOURS already remove.

Keyed on the structural signature (line-initial all-caps CONTACT followed only
by a personal name), never paper identity. A _CONTACT_NON_NAME_WORDS veto keeps
nav furniture ("CONTACT Details Below"). The orphaned "<City>, <Region>" tail is
removed ONLY by adjacency to a dropped opener -- never on its own shape, since a
bare "Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR" is ordinary prose (a test pins that it survives
alone). The wrapped pattern deliberately does NOT live in
_PAGE_FOOTER_LINE_PATTERNS: the generic any()-match would drop vetoed lines
before the veto branch could run.

2. KEYWORDS label/value split (sections/core.py)

The keywords section came out as 10 chars ('KEYWORDS\n\n') while its values
became the synthesized Introduction's opening line. The cut-at-first-"\n\n"
landed BETWEEN the label and its own values. General rule: a "cut at the first
separator" heuristic needs a post-condition on what the cut LEAVES, not only
where it lands.

render.py's _demote_metadata_label_headings blamed this on "R4 column-aware
extraction reorders the front-matter" -- false on both counts (the raw text has
label and values adjacent and in order, and "Introduction" does not occur in
that paper's source at all; the heading is synthesized). Comment corrected.

3. pytest had NO configuration (pyproject.toml)

A bare pytest walked tmp/ and collected 6 scratch files -> 10 collection ERRORs
and a test count that depended on leftover debris (run5=1962 vs run6=2295, not
comparable), defeating the project's "a shrinking test count is a failure"
tripwire. testpaths pinned -> stable 2199 = 2155 pre-existing + 44 new.

Verification
- 44 new tests, each watched FAILING against unfixed HEAD first.
- Contact guard-diff, production path, 127 docs incl. all 8 canaries:
  identical=125 changed=2 errors=0. Both changed docs are T&F papers; every
  removed line is genuine correspondence furniture. NO lines added anywhere.
  Surfaced the same leak on chan_feldman, undetected across 5 prior AI sweeps.
- Keywords guard-diff, 156 docs incl. all 8 canaries:
  identical=155 changed=1 errors=0; the 1 is xiao, exactly the intended repair.
- Both guard-diffs verified their monkeypatch EFFECTIVE first, so a zero result
  is trustworthy rather than a false green.
- Suite on this exact tree: 2006 passed, 190 skipped, 3 xfailed, 0 failed.
- Golden snapshots confirmed section-identical BEFORE regenerating; the diff is

recent_commits.message: docpluck-iterate: add rule 20a — how to survey, and when a survey cannot help
recent_commits.body:
Rule 20 says "survey the corpus before you write a threshold". Run 5 obeyed it
and still got the survey wrong TWICE, in opposite directions, so the rule needed
the missing half: how to build a survey whose number means anything.

(a) Survey through the REAL entry point. The W0i survey fed raw pdftotext lines
    through a function that production only ever calls on Camelot table cells,
    and reported ~85 hits in 10 papers -- including a paper's TITLE. The
    production render for that same paper had ZERO. Overstated ~10x; reporting it
    would have described a catastrophe that does not exist and over-engineered
    the guard to match. Red flag encoded: a hit-rate wildly above the audit that
    motivated the work means the harness is over-broad.

(b) A ZERO result must be falsified before it is believed. The first W0d survey
    returned zero firings corpus-wide -- a comfortable all-clear that was pure
    artifact (W0d runs whole-document; the raw-text channel puts each cell on its
    own line, so an estimate and its CI never share a line).

(c) Prefer a GUARD-DIFF over a hit count: render twice with the change toggled,
    so every difference is attributable. Both run-5 fixes shipped on exactly that
    evidence. When a full double-render is too slow, pre-filter by a stated
    criterion and report BOTH numbers so coverage stays auditable.

Plus the boundary condition that retires an entire approach family: if the thing
you are detecting occurs on exactly ONE row, no vote/follower/corroboration rule
can recover it. Counting the populated occurrences first would have saved two
prototypes on the plos_med column loss.

All references and factual claims re-verified against the tree before commit.

recent_commits.message: docs(findings): the plos_med column loss has a STRUCTURAL ceiling, not a threshold one
recent_commits.body:
Probed the follower/identity direction the survey pointed to (require the wide
row's column starts to be corroborated by the rows below). The classes do
separate -- furniture scores a clean 0.00, the real header 0.20 -- but 0.20 is
far too weak to found a threshold on, and per-column corroboration explains why:

    x=36.0 -> 15/15    x=284.7 -> 4/15    x=369.3 -> 3/15
    x=442.8 -> 1/15    x=549.8 -> 0/15  <- the P-value column

The rightmost column has ZERO corroboration anywhere in the table. Rel. risk and
P value are populated on exactly ONE row (the aggregate); the other 11 are
indented sub-rows that legitimately leave them blank. No vote-, follower-, or
corroboration-based rule can recover a column that occurs once -- the repetition
those algorithms need is not in the document.

So a geometry-only repair is impossible for this class, which retires the whole
family of attempts rather than inviting a fifth. What remains viable is evidence
from outside the geometry: header-TEXT typing (the header cells are recognisable
statistic labels, so they declare the column count directly), gated to
caption-anchored regions so it cannot fire on the ~1,700 prose pages the earlier
survey surfaced; or feeding header-derived x-positions to Camelot as explicit
columns. Both still need the 101-PDF guard-diff and canary sweep.

Records the cheap early check that would have saved two prototypes: count how
many rows populate the missing column; if it is 1, no geometric rule applies.

recent_commits.message: docs(findings): header-seeding PROTOTYPED then REJECTED by the corpus survey
recent_commits.body:
The proposed repair for plos_med T3's lost statistics columns -- seed boundaries
from the widest row, since the header declares every column -- was prototyped and
recovers the 5-column grid exactly. The vote tally shows the defect in one line:
the four TRUE boundaries carry 5, 13, 2 and 2 votes against a threshold of 7, so
exactly one clears it and the rule deletes all four.

The corpus survey then killed the fix. Scanning all 152 PDFs for the shape returns
1,707 pages, dominated by ordinary PROSE (modal=1 widest=4 wide_rows=1/22).
Inspecting one directly shows the "widest row" is a PAGE FOOTER --
"JAMANetworkOpen.2023;6(5): | (Reprinted) | May31,2023 | 10/12" -- above a
REFERENCES list. Seeding from it would fabricate a 4-column table out of a
bibliography on ~1,700 pages; the tail ("lost 29 columns") is the same artifact.

So the failing signal is not sparsity but IDENTITY: which row is actually a
header. A viable fix must establish that first (inside a caption-anchored region,
followed by data rows sharing its column starts -- _row_is_header is the natural
home) and be re-measured against this same 1,707-page population.

Second geometric shortcut rejected for this defect class, fourth across the
row-cluster family. Each looked excellent on its motivating paper; measurement,
not review, killed them. Recorded as a project lesson: print the winning row's
TEXT, not just its column count -- a footer, a running header and a wrapped
caption all look like "wide rows" to geometry.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): refuse a sign flip against a CI that cannot hold a negative (v2.4.123)
recent_commits.body:
docpluck rendered an IMPOSSIBLE F-statistic. maier Table 9's row is

    Target article | 1, 114 | 2.00 | .16 | N/A | .02 | [.00, .09]

-- an F, its p, its partial eta-squared, and the CI OF THE ETA-SQUARED. W0d
(recover_minus_via_ci_pairing) repairs a font corruption where a minus is read
as '2', accepting the flip when the corrected value lands inside a paired CI and
the literal does not. It paired the F-statistic with the eta-squared's CI: -.00
is inside [.00, .09] and 2.00 is not, so it fired, and the render carried

    F = -.00

An F-statistic is a ratio of sums of squares -- non-negative by construction --
so the output was not merely wrong but arithmetically impossible. Both text
channels confirm the source reads 2.00; the library manufactured the sign.

Fix: refuse the pairing when the CI's LOWER bound is >= 0. A wholly non-negative
interval cannot contain a negative, so containment is satisfiable only
degenerately (-.00 clipping the zero edge), which is evidence of MIS-PAIRING
rather than corruption. Keying on the interval's arithmetic instead of on F
specifically covers every non-negative statistic that can sit beside a
non-negative CI (F, chi-square, R2, eta2, odds ratios, variance components)
without enumerating them, and cannot disarm a genuine recovery -- a truly
negative estimate always has a CI admitting negatives.

Evidence:
- tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- all 31 pre-existing W0d tests stay green, incl. the efendic B-column
  recoveries the rule exists for;
- corpus guard-diff, all 152 PDFs rendered twice (guard on vs off):
  2 false positives removed (the maier article and its ESCIcheck duplicate),
  0 regressions, every other paper byte-identical;
- suite 1962 passed, 3 xfail (the P1 table defects stay armed).

Companion to the REJECTED W0b-col recovery: that failed because column consensus
is not per-record evidence. This is the converse -- per-record containment IS the
right evidence, but only when the record paired is the right one. A containment
test silently assumes the CI belongs to the token it pairs with; verify that is
arithmetically possible first.

Found by the run-5 canary audit against the AI multimodal gold.

recent_commits.message: docs(audit): DP-3 cross-project adjudication — verdict upheld, MECHANISM REFUTED
recent_commits.body:
First item of the queued cross-project re-audit, chosen for blast radius: a
docpluck->ESCIcheck REPLY document where one project told another "not our defect".

REPLY_FROM_DOCPLUCK_2026-06-25 stated the root cause as "the eta-squared-p glyph
lives in a font with no ToUnicode CMap (NotoSerif-Regular uni:no), so both pdftotext
AND pdfplumber decode it as a space". Measured on collabra.90203 p.1:

- NotoSerif-Regular carries 561 char objects on that page and ALL 561 are the SPACE
  character -- it is the document's space font, not a symbol font.
- Its space widths are 2.08-3.90pt (mean 2.43); ZERO exceed 5pt, while the symbol's
  ink spans 7.98pt. No NotoSerif space is wide enough to be the symbol.
- The only char object near the gap is a NotoSerif space at x0=229.97 -- the ordinary
  space BEFORE the '=' at x=232.31, i.e. after the symbol, not in place of it.
- The symbol is 4 filled bezier curves (fill=True, no fontname) with NO char object.

So the verdict (OCR/shape-recognition tier for body prose) is RIGHT, but the stated
mechanism is REFUTED. Codex on why that still causes harm: the rationale teaches the
wrong failure mode, so a consumer would attempt ToUnicode recovery, glyph-name
mapping, extractor tuning or post-processing NotoSerif spaces -- all of which target
the ordinary space before '=' and can never recover drawn curves. The distinction
that matters is "text encoded badly" vs "ink that is not text".

PROPAGATION CONFIRMED. REPLY_TO_DOCPLUCK_2026-06-26 records ESCIcheck replying "we
confirmed your OCR-tier won't-fix: the prose reads '( = .000...)' with no eta
anywhere" -- the identical circular check. A wrong rationale crossed the repo
boundary and was ratified by the receiving project using the same flawed method.
That is exactly the shape this audit exists to catch.

Both documents now carry correction blocks (in ESCIcheckapp, a separate repo). The
table-side fields.eta2 binding is unaffected and remains correct. A deterministic
vector-path recogniser remains a viable NON-OCR route.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize,sections): wrapped-CONTACT strip + KEYWORDS label/value split (v2.4.124)
recent_commits.body:
Publisher furniture was splitting a sentence in half, and a keyword list was
being read as the Introduction's first sentence.

NORMALIZATION_VERSION -> 1.9.49; SECTIONING_VERSION -> 1.2.4.

1. Wrapped-CONTACT block (normalize.py, P0)

xiao_2021_crsp rendered the T&F correspondence footer INSIDE a body sentence:
"The target and the / CONTACT Gilad Feldman / Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR /
competitor form a core choice set". The v2.4.6 rule requires CONTACT + name +
email on ONE line; T&F column-wraps the block so each lands on its own line.

Four of the block's six lines were ALREADY stripped by sibling patterns, so
this was a PARTIAL strip -- worse than none, because it removes exactly the
lines that made the block recognisable as furniture and welds the residue into
prose. When auditing a strip rule, check what its NEIGHBOURS already remove.

Keyed on the structural signature (line-initial all-caps CONTACT followed only
by a personal name), never paper identity. A _CONTACT_NON_NAME_WORDS veto keeps
nav furniture ("CONTACT Details Below"). The orphaned "<City>, <Region>" tail is
removed ONLY by adjacency to a dropped opener -- never on its own shape, since a
bare "Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR" is ordinary prose (a test pins that it survives
alone). The wrapped pattern deliberately does NOT live in
_PAGE_FOOTER_LINE_PATTERNS: the generic any()-match would drop vetoed lines
before the veto branch could run.

2. KEYWORDS label/value split (sections/core.py)

The keywords section came out as 10 chars ('KEYWORDS\n\n') while its values
became the synthesized Introduction's opening line. The cut-at-first-"\n\n"
landed BETWEEN the label and its own values. General rule: a "cut at the first
separator" heuristic needs a post-condition on what the cut LEAVES, not only
where it lands.

render.py's _demote_metadata_label_headings blamed this on "R4 column-aware
extraction reorders the front-matter" -- false on both counts (the raw text has
label and values adjacent and in order, and "Introduction" does not occur in
that paper's source at all; the heading is synthesized). Comment corrected.

3. pytest had NO configuration (pyproject.toml)

A bare pytest walked tmp/ and collected 6 scratch files -> 10 collection ERRORs
and a test count that depended on leftover debris (run5=1962 vs run6=2295, not
comparable), defeating the project's "a shrinking test count is a failure"
tripwire. testpaths pinned -> stable 2199 = 2155 pre-existing + 44 new.

Verification
- 44 new tests, each watched FAILING against unfixed HEAD first.
- Contact guard-diff, production path, 127 docs incl. all 8 canaries:
  identical=125 changed=2 errors=0. Both changed docs are T&F papers; every
  removed line is genuine correspondence furniture. NO lines added anywhere.
  Surfaced the same leak on chan_feldman, undetected across 5 prior AI sweeps.
- Keywords guard-diff, 156 docs incl. all 8 canaries:
  identical=155 changed=1 errors=0; the 1 is xiao, exactly the intended repair.
- Both guard-diffs verified their monkeypatch EFFECTIVE first, so a zero result
  is trustworthy rather than a false green.
- Suite on this exact tree: 2006 passed, 190 skipped, 3 xfailed, 0 failed.
- Golden snapshots confirmed section-identical BEFORE regenerating; the diff is
  one version line per file, no boundary moved.

  verifier confirms both repairs LANDED with no over-stripping. All 8 remain

recent_commits.message: docpluck-iterate: add rule 20a — how to survey, and when a survey cannot help
recent_commits.body:
Rule 20 says "survey the corpus before you write a threshold". Run 5 obeyed it
and still got the survey wrong TWICE, in opposite directions, so the rule needed
the missing half: how to build a survey whose number means anything.

(a) Survey through the REAL entry point. The W0i survey fed raw pdftotext lines
    through a function that production only ever calls on Camelot table cells,
    and reported ~85 hits in 10 papers -- including a paper's TITLE. The
    production render for that same paper had ZERO. Overstated ~10x; reporting it
    would have described a catastrophe that does not exist and over-engineered
    the guard to match. Red flag encoded: a hit-rate wildly above the audit that
    motivated the work means the harness is over-broad.

(b) A ZERO result must be falsified before it is believed. The first W0d survey
    returned zero firings corpus-wide -- a comfortable all-clear that was pure
    artifact (W0d runs whole-document; the raw-text channel puts each cell on its
    own line, so an estimate and its CI never share a line).

(c) Prefer a GUARD-DIFF over a hit count: render twice with the change toggled,
    so every difference is attributable. Both run-5 fixes shipped on exactly that
    evidence. When a full double-render is too slow, pre-filter by a stated
    criterion and report BOTH numbers so coverage stays auditable.

Plus the boundary condition that retires an entire approach family: if the thing
you are detecting occurs on exactly ONE row, no vote/follower/corroboration rule
can recover it. Counting the populated occurrences first would have saved two
prototypes on the plos_med column loss.

All references and factual claims re-verified against the tree before commit.

recent_commits.body:
Probed the follower/identity direction the survey pointed to (require the wide
row's column starts to be corroborated by the rows below). The classes do
separate -- furniture scores a clean 0.00, the real header 0.20 -- but 0.20 is
far too weak to found a threshold on, and per-column corroboration explains why:

    x=36.0 -> 15/15    x=284.7 -> 4/15    x=369.3 -> 3/15
    x=442.8 -> 1/15    x=549.8 -> 0/15  <- the P-value column

The rightmost column has ZERO corroboration anywhere in the table. Rel. risk and
P value are populated on exactly ONE row (the aggregate); the other 11 are
indented sub-rows that legitimately leave them blank. No vote-, follower-, or
corroboration-based rule can recover a column that occurs once -- the repetition
those algorithms need is not in the document.

So a geometry-only repair is impossible for this class, which retires the whole
family of attempts rather than inviting a fifth. What remains viable is evidence
from outside the geometry: header-TEXT typing (the header cells are recognisable
statistic labels, so they declare the column count directly), gated to
caption-anchored regions so it cannot fire on the ~1,700 prose pages the earlier
survey surfaced; or feeding header-derived x-positions to Camelot as explicit
columns. Both still need the 101-PDF guard-diff and canary sweep.

Records the cheap early check that would have saved two prototypes: count how
many rows populate the missing column; if it is 1, no geometric rule applies.

recent_commits.message: docs(findings): header-seeding PROTOTYPED then REJECTED by the corpus survey
recent_commits.body:
The proposed repair for plos_med T3's lost statistics columns -- seed boundaries
from the widest row, since the header declares every column -- was prototyped and
recovers the 5-column grid exactly. The vote tally shows the defect in one line:
the four TRUE boundaries carry 5, 13, 2 and 2 votes against a threshold of 7, so
exactly one clears it and the rule deletes all four.

The corpus survey then killed the fix. Scanning all 152 PDFs for the shape returns
1,707 pages, dominated by ordinary PROSE (modal=1 widest=4 wide_rows=1/22).
Inspecting one directly shows the "widest row" is a PAGE FOOTER --
"JAMANetworkOpen.2023;6(5): | (Reprinted) | May31,2023 | 10/12" -- above a
REFERENCES list. Seeding from it would fabricate a 4-column table out of a
bibliography on ~1,700 pages; the tail ("lost 29 columns") is the same artifact.

So the failing signal is not sparsity but IDENTITY: which row is actually a
header. A viable fix must establish that first (inside a caption-anchored region,
followed by data rows sharing its column starts -- _row_is_header is the natural
home) and be re-measured against this same 1,707-page population.

Second geometric shortcut rejected for this defect class, fourth across the
row-cluster family. Each looked excellent on its motivating paper; measurement,
not review, killed them. Recorded as a project lesson: print the winning row's
TEXT, not just its column count -- a footer, a running header and a wrapped
caption all look like "wide rows" to geometry.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): refuse a sign flip against a CI that cannot hold a negative (v2.4.123)
recent_commits.body:
docpluck rendered an IMPOSSIBLE F-statistic. maier Table 9's row is

    Target article | 1, 114 | 2.00 | .16 | N/A | .02 | [.00, .09]

-- an F, its p, its partial eta-squared, and the CI OF THE ETA-SQUARED. W0d
(recover_minus_via_ci_pairing) repairs a font corruption where a minus is read
as '2', accepting the flip when the corrected value lands inside a paired CI and
the literal does not. It paired the F-statistic with the eta-squared's CI: -.00
is inside [.00, .09] and 2.00 is not, so it fired, and the render carried

    F = -.00

An F-statistic is a ratio of sums of squares -- non-negative by construction --
so the output was not merely wrong but arithmetically impossible. Both text
channels confirm the source reads 2.00; the library manufactured the sign.

Fix: refuse the pairing when the CI's LOWER bound is >= 0. A wholly non-negative
interval cannot contain a negative, so containment is satisfiable only
degenerately (-.00 clipping the zero edge), which is evidence of MIS-PAIRING
rather than corruption. Keying on the interval's arithmetic instead of on F
specifically covers every non-negative statistic that can sit beside a
non-negative CI (F, chi-square, R2, eta2, odds ratios, variance components)
without enumerating them, and cannot disarm a genuine recovery -- a truly
negative estimate always has a CI admitting negatives.

Evidence:
- tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- all 31 pre-existing W0d tests stay green, incl. the efendic B-column
  recoveries the rule exists for;
- corpus guard-diff, all 152 PDFs rendered twice (guard on vs off):
  2 false positives removed (the maier article and its ESCIcheck duplicate),
  0 regressions, every other paper byte-identical;
- suite 1962 passed, 3 xfail (the P1 table defects stay armed).

Companion to the REJECTED W0b-col recovery: that failed because column consensus
is not per-record evidence. This is the converse -- per-record containment IS the
right evidence, but only when the record paired is the right one. A containment
test silently assumes the CI belongs to the token it pairs with; verify that is
arithmetically possible first.

Found by the run-5 canary audit against the AI multimodal gold.

from the widest row, since the header declares every column -- was prototyped and

not review, killed them. Recorded as a project lesson: print the winning row's
TEXT, not just its column count -- a footer, a running header and a wrapped

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): refuse a sign flip against a CI that cannot hold a negative (v2.4.123)
recent_commits.body:
docpluck rendered an IMPOSSIBLE F-statistic. maier Table 9's row is

    Target article | 1, 114 | 2.00 | .16 | N/A | .02 | [.00, .09]

-- an F, its p, its partial eta-squared, and the CI OF THE ETA-SQUARED. W0d
(recover_minus_via_ci_pairing) repairs a font corruption where a minus is read
as '2', accepting the flip when the corrected value lands inside a paired CI and
the literal does not. It paired the F-statistic with the eta-squared's CI: -.00
is inside [.00, .09] and 2.00 is not, so it fired, and the render carried

    F = -.00

An F-statistic is a ratio of sums of squares -- non-negative by construction --
so the output was not merely wrong but arithmetically impossible. Both text
channels confirm the source reads 2.00; the library manufactured the sign.

Fix: refuse the pairing when the CI's LOWER bound is >= 0. A wholly non-negative
interval cannot contain a negative, so containment is satisfiable only
degenerately (-.00 clipping the zero edge), which is evidence of MIS-PAIRING
rather than corruption. Keying on the interval's arithmetic instead of on F
specifically covers every non-negative statistic that can sit beside a
non-negative CI (F, chi-square, R2, eta2, odds ratios, variance components)
without enumerating them, and cannot disarm a genuine recovery -- a truly
negative estimate always has a CI admitting negatives.

Evidence:
- tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- all 31 pre-existing W0d tests stay green, incl. the efendic B-column
  recoveries the rule exists for;
- corpus guard-diff, all 152 PDFs rendered twice (guard on vs off):
  2 false positives removed (the maier article and its ESCIcheck duplicate),
  0 regressions, every other paper byte-identical;
- suite 1962 passed, 3 xfail (the P1 table defects stay armed).

Companion to the REJECTED W0b-col recovery: that failed because column consensus
is not per-record evidence. This is the converse -- per-record containment IS the
right evidence, but only when the record paired is the right one. A containment
test silently assumes the CI belongs to the token it pairs with; verify that is
arithmetically possible first.

Found by the run-5 canary audit against the AI multimodal gold.

recent_commits.message: docs(findings): measure WHY plos_med T3 loses its columns — hierarchical sub-rows
recent_commits.body:
Probing _find_stable_column_boundaries on the real Table-3 band replaces the
earlier speculation (which guessed at midpoint scatter and the region path) with
a measurement, and it kills the proposed fix:

  WORD path: valid_rows=13 threshold=7 -> stable boundaries: [] -> 1 column
  BUCKETED(3/5/8pt): still 2 columns

The word path finds ZERO stable boundaries, so the region path is NOT the
culprit. The cause is the table's shape: Table 3 is hierarchical -- the header
and one aggregate row carry all 5 columns, while 11 of 13 rows are indented
sub-rows carrying only 3 (desaturation | 3/5 | 1/4). The Rel. risk and P value
columns appear in 2/13 rows = 15%, far below COLUMN_STABILITY_FRACTION = 0.6, so
they can never reach the vote threshold. Bucketing cannot help -- the votes do
not exist to be bucketed.

Lowering the fraction is explicitly NOT the fix (rule 20): 0.6 guards against
spurious boundaries from ragged prose rows, and a threshold admitting a 15%
column admits noise corpus-wide. The correct signature is that a column declared
by the HEADER is real even when most rows leave it empty -- seed boundaries from
the header rather than letting a majority vote delete them. That is an algorithm
change to a shared detector, so it gets its own gated cycle.

Also removes the now-superseded speculative section so the doc does not
contradict its own measurement, and records the class as a project lesson: a
stability-fraction vote assumes every column is populated in most rows, which
hierarchical/sub-row tables (common in clinical papers) violate by construction --
and the failure is silent, looking like a complete table with fewer columns.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): a range bound is a number, not an interaction operator (v2.4.122)
recent_commits.body:
W0i's x-as-3 glyph recovery was rewriting RANGE BOUNDS as an operator inside
Camelot table cells. chan_feldman's Table-2 note rendered

    "Avoidance behaviour scores ranged from x to 15"

for a source that reads "from 3 to 15" -- the library DELETED a published scale
bound and wrote an operator in its place. Both text channels confirm the source
says 3; the raw-text channel rendered the same sentence correctly a hundred
lines earlier, so one document carried the same fact right and wrong at once.

Not paper-specific: any "from 3 to N" / "between 3 and N" reaching a table cell
was affected, in any publisher's paper.

Root cause: W0i's only pre-digit guard was _TIMES_REFERENCE_WORD_RE, a list of
reference NOUNS (Model|Study|Table|Figure|...) that makes "Model 3 predictor" a
genuine ordinal. "from" is not a reference noun, so the guard had nothing to
say, while "from 3 to" matches W0i's letter-space-3-space-letter signature
exactly. A vocabulary list cannot defend a grammatical position -- it is always
missing the next word.

Fix: guard on the grammatical FRAME instead. A range is from|between BEFORE the
digit AND to|and|through|until AFTER it, with BOTH halves required -- a lone
trailing "to" could be a wrapped predictor ("Attitude 3 to risk"), and a lone
leading "from" is likewise ambiguous. A frame generalises across publishers.

Evidence:
- new tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- full-corpus pdftotext sweep (all 152 PDFs): 8 range-frame-with-3 sites across
  5 distinct articles, out of 380 range frames overall -- all 5 pinned as
  regression cases. The sweep is why the guard covers "between ... and": maier's
  Bayes factors and bmc_med_3's lesion diameters use it, and a from-only guard
  would have left them exposed;
- targeted production-path guard-diff (each paper rendered twice, guard on vs
  off, so every difference is attributable to this change): 1 false positive
  removed, 0 regressions, all 8 canaries byte-identical;
- suite: 1959 passed, 3 xfail (the two P1 pinned table defects stay armed).

Found by the run-5 cycle-1 canary audit against the AI multimodal gold.

recent_commits.message: docpluck-iterate: add hard rule 20 — survey the corpus before writing a threshold
recent_commits.body:
The run-4 v2.4.120/121 session's most expensive mistake and its most valuable
save both trace to this missing rule. The skill had no guidance to validate a
threshold/ratio/signature against the corpus BEFORE implementing it.

its motivating paper (chan_feldman T3 3->22 rows, T2 0->108 cells) and broke 9

distinct_y, sub-line width fraction) were each falsified in minutes against the
101-PDF corpus instead of via a revert.

The rule also encodes the label-verification half, which is where the real trap
sits: hand-picked extremes ALWAYS separate, so only the decision band matters,
and labelling by provenance is a guess. Verifying the band's labels by reading
them reversed this session's conclusion TWICE before the third reading settled
it. And it requires reporting the MARGIN, not just the ordering — a correct
ordering with a 0.019 gap on six points is a rejection, not a fix.

prove the signature actually discriminates before shipping it.

recent_commits.message: docs(findings): 4 geometric chain-merge discriminators tested and rejected; period-aware column overlap is the best candidate but still unsafe
recent_commits.body:
Continues the corpus-driven falsification of the row-cluster chain-merge fix.

REJECTED (all measured corpus-wide or on verified cases):
  - row span:            legit rows reach 94pt+ (xiao T4 r2)
  - max internal y-gap:  9.0pt legit vs 9.5pt chain — indistinguishable
  - distinct_y count:    continuous 2->50, classes interleave (legit 26 > chain 23)
  - subline width frac:  both classes 0.42-0.54, chain sits BETWEEN legit rows
                         (raw widths looked separable, 202-238 vs 84-150, but the
                         chain-merge regions are simply wider — normalising kills it)
  - start_at_left:       46% in BOTH classes

BEST CANDIDATE, still unsafe: column-boundary consistency. Mean Jaccard of
x-start buckets between CONSECUTIVE sub-lines gives chain 0.008-0.023 vs legit
0.21-0.28 — except xiao T4 r2 scores 0.017, deep in the chain band. That is the
exact row whose mis-splitting broke 9 tests, so this variant would repeat the
failure. It alternates data lines with CI-continuation lines, so consecutive
sub-lines never share columns but the pattern is strictly PERIODIC.

A period-aware variant (best mean Jaccard over lags 1-3) fixes xiao (0.692) and
separates the rest — but ip_feldman T10 r1 (chain) reaches 0.251 against chan T6
r2 (legit) at 0.270. A 0.019 margin on six hand-picked rows will not survive the
corpus; it needs the same survey that killed distinct_y, over rows whose class is
VERIFIED rather than assumed, and must be rejected if the margin does not widen.

Explicit guidance added: do NOT attempt a fifth geometric threshold. Remaining
viable directions are content typing and split-then-re-merge on column occupancy.

No library code changes.

recent_commits.message: docs(findings): chain-merge scope is wider; distinct_y threshold tested and REJECTED
recent_commits.body:
Two updates to the row-cluster chain-merge finding, both from measurement.

SCOPE IS WIDER. The chain merge is not only chan_feldman's problem — it is also
the blocker for maier Table 5, whose char grid row 0 spans 124.3pt across 49
distinct y-levels with the caption, header and every data row interleaved
CHARACTER-BY-CHARACTER into one cell ('TabENToxloetpailn5ilct.ietrHlv'). The
v2.4.121 composite clean-data fix did NOT recover T5 (still 0x0) because the grid
is destroyed at clustering time, before any guard sees it. So this gates a
meaningful slice of the table backlog, not one paper.

DISTINCT_Y THRESHOLD REJECTED. distinct_y looked like a clean discriminator on
three hand-picked cases (chain 43/49 vs legit 13). A corpus-wide survey of all
199 tall rows killed it: the distribution is CONTINUOUS from 2 to 50 with no gap,
and hand-inspecting the decision band shows the classes genuinely interleave —
chan T4 r2 (dy=23) and chan T6 r2 (dy=26) are LEGITIMATE stacked categorical
rows, while ip_feldman T10 r1 (dy=27) is a real chain merge fusing '.29*** -.21***
.07' with Discussion prose. A legitimate row at 26 sits above a chain merge at 23.

Also recorded as a caution against labelling by assumption: two rows I first
called legitimate were not (sci_rep_2 T1 r13 is absorbed body prose; chen T9 r1
is the sparse label 'Study 2:'). Verifying them flipped the conclusion twice.

Conclusion: row height, gap size and y-level count are ALL insufficient. The
discriminator must use content or column occupancy, not geometry alone.

No library code changes.

recent_commits.message: fix(tables,normalize): grid-guard false negatives + a 50x ReDoS (v2.4.121)
recent_commits.body:
TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION -> 2.4.10. NORMALIZATION_VERSION deliberately
unchanged: the normalize fix is complexity-only, matching is byte-identical.

Two false-negative classes in the guard that decides whether a whitespace/char
grid is a real DATA table:

(a) _CAPTION_LABEL_RE was UNANCHORED, so a mid-sentence CROSS-REFERENCE in a
    footnote/prose cell ("...al. (2007) in Table 8.", "...in Figure 2. We
    summarized...") read as an absorbed caption and condemned the whole grid.
    An absorbed caption always BEGINS its cell; a reference has sentence text
    before it. Anchored to ^\s*, matching the discipline
    camelot_extract._CAPTION_ROW_PATTERN already documents (its comment notes
    anchoring is why an inline "see Table 2" does not match).

(b) the clean-data-cell test matched a SINGLE numeric token, so every
    multi-token APA COMPOSITE scored as non-data: 2.84 [1.89] (mean [SD]),
    3.47 [1.23] (170) (mean [SD] (n)), 2.84 +/- 1.89, 0.42***. A descriptives
    table built from them scored clean_data_rows=0 and was discarded as prose.
    Replaced the shape regex with a NUMERIC-DOMINANCE test (_cell_is_clean_data:
    digit-bearing AND free of substantive words), which generalises instead of
    chasing each composite with another alternation. The prose side is unmoved,
    so absorbed body text is still rejected.

101-PDF guard-diff: 24 tables recover (up from 20 at v2.4.120), 0 regressed,
0 foreign-caption acceptances.

A SECOND quadratic regex, and why the first fix looked complete but wasn't:
v2.4.120 bounded _CI_UPPER_DROPPED_RE and reported the ReDoS resolved. It was
not — normalize_text still scaled ~4-5x per doubling. It was missed because the
check was an absolute WALL-CLOCK budget, which passed alone and failed only
under parallel load, so it read as flakiness. Rewritten as a SCALING RATIO
(load-independent: contention inflates both measurements together) it failed
consistently, turning noise into signal.

Instrumenting every COMPILED pattern's .sub() via re.compile interception (a
module-level sweep misses these — they live inside a list literal, and reported
0.000s) attributed 3.165s of 3.7s at n=20000 to the Royal Society running-footer
pattern in _WATERMARK_PATTERNS, whose leading unbounded \d+ starts a match
attempt at every digit and then fails. Bounding it to \d{1,6} (a page number is
never longer) is ~1370x faster on the pattern (4.53s -> 0.0033s) and ~50x
end-to-end (normalize_text 4.85s -> 0.044s at n=20000), now genuinely linear at
~2.0x per doubling, with both real footer forms matched identically. A
lookahead-anchored variant was tried first and MEASURED WORSE (6.4s vs 3.2s) —
discarded rather than reasoned about.

This permanently removes the flakiness from
test_regex_no_catastrophic_backtracking, which prior handoffs recorded as a
load-sensitive perf test. It was a real, long-standing performance defect all
along. Full suite also runs ~10 min faster (24:51 vs 37:19).

Suite: 2218 passed, 194 skipped, 3 xfailed, 0 failed.

recent_commits.message: test(tables): pin the _cluster_into_rows chain-merge defect (attempted fix REVERTED)
recent_commits.body:
_cluster_into_rows measures the y-gap to the PREVIOUS WORD, not the row's anchor.
Words sort by (top, x0), so in a table with wrapped or vertically staggered cells
the running 'previous top' creeps forward in sub-threshold steps and the threshold
is never crossed — an unbounded chain merge. chan_feldman Table 3 holds 266 words
at 47 distinct y-positions with 0.3-7.4pt gaps against an 11.4pt threshold, and
clusters into 3 rows spanning 240pt: a 10-row table smeared into 3, which then
fails the grid guards on its own 'merits' and falls to the truncating raw_text
fallback.

The anchor-relative fix was implemented and REVERTED. In isolation it looked
excellent (chan T3 3->22 rows; T2 0->108 cells; T9 0->14 cells; maier T8/T11
gained cells) but it broke 9 real-PDF tests across 4 files, because a real row
can legitimately be TALL: xiao Table 4's row 2 spans 94.4pt as a multi-line
stacked data block, and a hard anchor cap shatters it. The previous-word test
under-splits; a naive anchor cap over-splits. Neither rule alone is correct.

Ships the reproduction as xfail(strict) so the defect stays visible and a correct
fix XPASSes loudly, plus three plain-assert companions pinning behaviour that must
not regress while it is solved. FINDINGS doc records the measurements and three
candidate directions (re-merge on shared column occupancy; explicit chain-merge
signature detection; derive the row grid from the most stable column).

No library code changes — the tree is byte-identical to v2.4.120.

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): a table's own caption no longer condemns its own table (v2.4.120)
recent_commits.body:
RC-T cycle 4. _whitespace_grid_is_clean rejects any grid containing a
"Table N."/"Figure N." cell — the signature of a region that absorbed a
NEIGHBOURING table's caption. But _region_for_caption builds every region as
_union(caption_bbox, geom_bbox), so a caption-anchored region ALWAYS contains
its own caption by construction. The guard therefore condemned EVERY region
grid: whitespace_cells returned 0 cells corpus-wide (19/19 chan_feldman+maier
regions) and each table fell to the raw_text fallback, which truncates rows.
The guard's own comment said the marker proves the region absorbed "an adjacent
table's (or its own) caption" — the "or its own" clause was the bug.

The exemption is IDENTITY-based, not position-based: the anchoring caption's
number is threaded from the region spec / region.caption_match into the guard,
and a caption cell is exempt only when it names THAT exact number, sits in a
leading row, and is the first such match — per-CELL, and opt-in so the
auto-detect path keeps the strict legacy behaviour.

A position-only draft was written and REJECTED in cross-model review (codex);
all three of its holes reproduced locally: a neighbour's caption in a leading
row blessed as "own" (publishing another table's data), (r,c) sort order picking
the leftmost caption on side-by-side pages, and a whole-ROW exemption letting a
second Table/Figure caption ride along. Each is pinned by a regression test.

101-PDF guard-diff: 20 tables recover, 0 regressed, 0 foreign-caption
acceptances. Recovery spans ip_feldman, jdm_.2023.15, korbmacher, maier,
am_sociol_rev and socius — not just the papers that motivated the cycle.

Also in this commit (leave-nothing-behind):

* ReDoS in normalize._CI_UPPER_DROPPED_RE. The intermittently-red
  test_regex_no_catastrophic_backtracking was recorded as merely load-sensitive;
  unloaded it took 2.3-6.9s against a 5s budget. The driver is the decimal
  atom's UNBOUNDED integer part (\d*\.\d+), quadratic on a long digit run
  (~4.6x per doubling). Bounding it to \d{0,20} is ~270x faster with identical
  matching. The decoration-gap hypothesis was measured and REJECTED first.
  NORMALIZATION_VERSION deliberately not bumped: complexity only, no behaviour
  change.

* test_chan_feldman_table8_ci_upper_signs_recovered re-targeted. It read the
  2bi/2bii hypothesis rows out of Table 8 and passed only because the pairing
  was wrong. The AI gold confirms Table 8 is the intercorrelation matrix and
  Table 9 is "Summary of statistical tests" — cycle 4 FIXED that pairing. Now
  selects the hypothesis grid by content, not a hard-coded label; the
  substantive negative-CI assertions are unchanged and gold-exact.

chan_feldman is NOT fixed by this cycle and keeps its xfail(strict), with the
corrected diagnosis: its regions genuinely absorb 2-column body prose and fail
the prose/clean-data guards on their own merits (the separate region prose-trim
cycle). Its T5/T8 rejections are CORRECT — those regions really do reach into
Table 9's caption at grid row 4, the guard's original defence case, intact.

Suite: 2184 passed, 193 skipped, 2 xfailed, 0 failed.

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): RC-T caption-tail walk — tables no longer drop their first rows (v2.4.119)
recent_commits.body:
The gated RC-T cycle (user-approved). `_extract_table_body_text`'s body_start
walk stepped break-to-break (preferring \n\n) with a 40-char window, so a
WRAPPED caption whose table body serializes column-by-column overshot the
caption's own terminator and SILENTLY DROPPED leading rows — chan_feldman
Table 3 lost its first four rows, Table 1 its first hypothesis row.

`_caption_tail_body_start` replaces it with a per-LINE walk carrying three
structural rules, each pinned by a corpus case the run-3 prototype regressed
on: whole-line terminator test (xiao T6), blank-line stop, and a max-wrap-lines
cap (amc_1 T3). Companion guards handle what the corrected walk now reaches:
`_skip_leading_nontable_junk` (leading figure caption / wrapped prose, bounded
+ terminated-only) and `_raw_text_is_page_furniture_only` (jama_open_1 T2
rendered ONLY a banner/title/date/"8/13"). `_line_is_body_prose` gains a
bibliography-row exemption.

Two corruptions the recovered rows EXPOSED (pre-existing, verified against a
v2.4.118 baseline — the data simply never reached the page before):
- S5b FFFD `>=` recovery was wired into channel 1 only, so plos_med Table 2's
  rows arrived as mojibake. Now wired into channel 3, with the document-
  consensus gate extended to count operators already present (unanimity kept).
- W0b-est: the estimate column is separated from its CI column by the SE
  column, so W0d's proximity window cannot span it (efendic T3 `21.34`).
  Estimates now pair with CIs POSITIONALLY, rewriting only when the corrected
  reading lands inside that CI and the literal one does not.

A recovery REJECTED before release: a `W0b-col` column-consensus rule flipped
efendic T5's `[2.42, 2.69]`, which the AI gold confirms is a GENUINELY POSITIVE
interval (Direction high-vs-low, est 2.56, p<.001) — it would have published a
sign-flipped effect. Removed; the case is pinned by a regression guard. The
pre-existing `_CORRUPT_CI_RE` was itself over-broad (matched ascending pairs,
asserting the wrong flip into existence) and is now descending-only. Standing
rule: a sign flip requires per-record evidence, never column membership.

Also: tests/conftest.py resolved fixtures under the dead ~/Dropbox/Vibe path,
so every articlerepo-keyed test SKIPPED silently (a green run that verified
nothing). Now VIBE_ROOT-aware.

prototype had 2); full suite 1872 passed (the one red is a load-sensitive
perf test that passes in isolation at 1.43s of a 5s budget); baseline 26/26;

told to check for it.

recent_commits.body:
ar_apa/JESP rendered `p < 05 (see Fig. 1)` — the significance threshold's
decimal point is drawn on the AdvGulliv broken-ToUnicode family and vanishes

significance-clause context) keep the 10-fold-wrong-number FP impossible on

are legitimate `P = 1` exact values, excluded by the operator guard). Wired
channels 1+3; NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.45.

recent_commits.message: docpluck-iterate: add hard rule 20 — survey the corpus before writing a threshold
recent_commits.body:
The run-4 v2.4.120/121 session's most expensive mistake and its most valuable
save both trace to this missing rule. The skill had no guidance to validate a
threshold/ratio/signature against the corpus BEFORE implementing it.

Cost when absent: the _cluster_into_rows anchor-relative fix looked excellent on
its motivating paper (chan_feldman T3 3->22 rows, T2 0->108 cells) and broke 9
real-PDF tests, because a legitimate row can be 94pt tall (xiao T4 r2).

Value when applied: four geometric discriminators (row span, max internal gap,
distinct_y, sub-line width fraction) were each falsified in minutes against the
101-PDF corpus instead of via a revert.

The rule also encodes the label-verification half, which is where the real trap
sits: hand-picked extremes ALWAYS separate, so only the decision band matters,
and labelling by provenance is a guess. Verifying the band's labels by reading
them reversed this session's conclusion TWICE before the third reading settled
it. And it requires reporting the MARGIN, not just the ordering — a correct
ordering with a 0.019 gap on six points is a rejection, not a fix.

Companion to rule 16: rule 16 says key on a structural signature; rule 20 says
prove the signature actually discriminates before shipping it.

Purely additive (2 insertions, 0 deletions). The concurrent session's
uncommitted Dropbox->Vibe path edit in this same file is deliberately NOT
included and remains in the working tree.

recent_commits.message: docs(findings): 4 geometric chain-merge discriminators tested and rejected; period-aware column overlap is the best candidate but still unsafe
recent_commits.body:
Continues the corpus-driven falsification of the row-cluster chain-merge fix.

REJECTED (all measured corpus-wide or on verified cases):
  - row span:            legit rows reach 94pt+ (xiao T4 r2)
  - max internal y-gap:  9.0pt legit vs 9.5pt chain — indistinguishable
  - distinct_y count:    continuous 2->50, classes interleave (legit 26 > chain 23)
  - subline width frac:  both classes 0.42-0.54, chain sits BETWEEN legit rows
                         (raw widths looked separable, 202-238 vs 84-150, but the
                         chain-merge regions are simply wider — normalising kills it)
  - start_at_left:       46% in BOTH classes

BEST CANDIDATE, still unsafe: column-boundary consistency. Mean Jaccard of
x-start buckets between CONSECUTIVE sub-lines gives chain 0.008-0.023 vs legit
0.21-0.28 — except xiao T4 r2 scores 0.017, deep in the chain band. That is the
exact row whose mis-splitting broke 9 tests, so this variant would repeat the
failure. It alternates data lines with CI-continuation lines, so consecutive
sub-lines never share columns but the pattern is strictly PERIODIC.

A period-aware variant (best mean Jaccard over lags 1-3) fixes xiao (0.692) and
separates the rest — but ip_feldman T10 r1 (chain) reaches 0.251 against chan T6
r2 (legit) at 0.270. A 0.019 margin on six hand-picked rows will not survive the
corpus; it needs the same survey that killed distinct_y, over rows whose class is
VERIFIED rather than assumed, and must be rejected if the margin does not widen.

Explicit guidance added: do NOT attempt a fifth geometric threshold. Remaining
viable directions are content typing and split-then-re-merge on column occupancy.

No library code changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: docs(findings): chain-merge scope is wider; distinct_y threshold tested and REJECTED
recent_commits.body:
Two updates to the row-cluster chain-merge finding, both from measurement.

SCOPE IS WIDER. The chain merge is not only chan_feldman's problem — it is also
the blocker for maier Table 5, whose char grid row 0 spans 124.3pt across 49
distinct y-levels with the caption, header and every data row interleaved
CHARACTER-BY-CHARACTER into one cell ('TabENToxloetpailn5ilct.ietrHlv'). The
v2.4.121 composite clean-data fix did NOT recover T5 (still 0x0) because the grid
is destroyed at clustering time, before any guard sees it. So this gates a
meaningful slice of the table backlog, not one paper.

DISTINCT_Y THRESHOLD REJECTED. distinct_y looked like a clean discriminator on
three hand-picked cases (chain 43/49 vs legit 13). A corpus-wide survey of all
199 tall rows killed it: the distribution is CONTINUOUS from 2 to 50 with no gap,
and hand-inspecting the decision band shows the classes genuinely interleave —
chan T4 r2 (dy=23) and chan T6 r2 (dy=26) are LEGITIMATE stacked categorical
rows, while ip_feldman T10 r1 (dy=27) is a real chain merge fusing '.29*** -.21***
.07' with Discussion prose. A legitimate row at 26 sits above a chain merge at 23.

Also recorded as a caution against labelling by assumption: two rows I first
called legitimate were not (sci_rep_2 T1 r13 is absorbed body prose; chen T9 r1
is the sparse label 'Study 2:'). Verifying them flipped the conclusion twice.

Conclusion: row height, gap size and y-level count are ALL insufficient. The

recent_commits.message: fix(tables,normalize): grid-guard false negatives + a 50x ReDoS (v2.4.121)
recent_commits.body:
TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION -> 2.4.10. NORMALIZATION_VERSION deliberately
unchanged: the normalize fix is complexity-only, matching is byte-identical.

Two false-negative classes in the guard that decides whether a whitespace/char
grid is a real DATA table:

(a) _CAPTION_LABEL_RE was UNANCHORED, so a mid-sentence CROSS-REFERENCE in a
    footnote/prose cell ("...al. (2007) in Table 8.", "...in Figure 2. We
    summarized...") read as an absorbed caption and condemned the whole grid.
    An absorbed caption always BEGINS its cell; a reference has sentence text
    before it. Anchored to ^\s*, matching the discipline
    camelot_extract._CAPTION_ROW_PATTERN already documents (its comment notes
    anchoring is why an inline "see Table 2" does not match).

(b) the clean-data-cell test matched a SINGLE numeric token, so every
    multi-token APA COMPOSITE scored as non-data: 2.84 [1.89] (mean [SD]),
    3.47 [1.23] (170) (mean [SD] (n)), 2.84 +/- 1.89, 0.42***. A descriptives
    table built from them scored clean_data_rows=0 and was discarded as prose.
    Replaced the shape regex with a NUMERIC-DOMINANCE test (_cell_is_clean_data:
    digit-bearing AND free of substantive words), which generalises instead of
    chasing each composite with another alternation. The prose side is unmoved,
    so absorbed body text is still rejected.

101-PDF guard-diff: 24 tables recover (up from 20 at v2.4.120), 0 regressed,
0 foreign-caption acceptances.

A SECOND quadratic regex, and why the first fix looked complete but wasn't:
v2.4.120 bounded _CI_UPPER_DROPPED_RE and reported the ReDoS resolved. It was
not — normalize_text still scaled ~4-5x per doubling. It was missed because the
check was an absolute WALL-CLOCK budget, which passed alone and failed only
under parallel load, so it read as flakiness. Rewritten as a SCALING RATIO
(load-independent: contention inflates both measurements together) it failed
consistently, turning noise into signal.

Instrumenting every COMPILED pattern's .sub() via re.compile interception (a
module-level sweep misses these — they live inside a list literal, and reported
0.000s) attributed 3.165s of 3.7s at n=20000 to the Royal Society running-footer
pattern in _WATERMARK_PATTERNS, whose leading unbounded \d+ starts a match
attempt at every digit and then fails. Bounding it to \d{1,6} (a page number is
never longer) is ~1370x faster on the pattern (4.53s -> 0.0033s) and ~50x
end-to-end (normalize_text 4.85s -> 0.044s at n=20000), now genuinely linear at
~2.0x per doubling, with both real footer forms matched identically. A
lookahead-anchored variant was tried first and MEASURED WORSE (6.4s vs 3.2s) —
discarded rather than reasoned about.

This permanently removes the flakiness from
test_regex_no_catastrophic_backtracking, which prior handoffs recorded as a
load-sensitive perf test. It was a real, long-standing performance defect all
along. Full suite also runs ~10 min faster (24:51 vs 37:19).

Suite: 2218 passed, 194 skipped, 3 xfailed, 0 failed.

recent_commits.body:
_pick_better_table selects between a caption's region-driven and auto-detected
candidates on STRUCTURAL SHAPE alone (column count, then cell count). Nothing
checks whether the winning grid's CONTENT is plausibly the caption's table.

maier Table 7 ('Perceived Impact (Extension): Descriptives') is a 3x5 grid in the
AI gold. With DOCPLUCK_DISABLE_CAMELOT=1 the raw_text channel captures it
GOLD-EXACT (all 15 values, 3.47 [1.23] (170) ... 3.12 [1.34] (1004)). With
Camelot enabled a 4x2 grid of DISCUSSION PROSE wins the shape comparison and
replaces it, so the render shows '### Table 7' with its caption and ZERO data
values. Silent, complete TEXT-LOSS of a real results table.

Traced to the channel: the winning grid is camelot_t18 — the LEGACY AUTO-DETECT
path. The content-plausibility guard runs only for region-path grids
(if id_prefix.startswith('region')), and feeding this exact grid to
_whitespace_grid_is_clean returns False — the guard WOULD have caught it,
auto-detect just never consults it. Widening that gate wholesale was already
tried and rejected (it discarded legitimate-but-imperfect auto-detect grids,
cog_emo T5/6/7), so the fix belongs at SELECTION time as a relative judgement
between candidates, not as a wider absolute gate.

that global pairing changes are net-harmful unless gated by a 101-PDF guard-diff
plus an AI-gold canary sweep (v2.4.6 global matching fixed bmc_med_3 but
regressed chan_feldman T6 and reshuffled ~24 papers).

raw_text channel still captures T7 correctly — which is what makes this a

recent_commits.message: test(tables): pin the _cluster_into_rows chain-merge defect (attempted fix REVERTED)
recent_commits.body:
_cluster_into_rows measures the y-gap to the PREVIOUS WORD, not the row's anchor.
Words sort by (top, x0), so in a table with wrapped or vertically staggered cells
the running 'previous top' creeps forward in sub-threshold steps and the threshold
is never crossed — an unbounded chain merge. chan_feldman Table 3 holds 266 words
at 47 distinct y-positions with 0.3-7.4pt gaps against an 11.4pt threshold, and
clusters into 3 rows spanning 240pt: a 10-row table smeared into 3, which then
fails the grid guards on its own 'merits' and falls to the truncating raw_text
fallback.

The anchor-relative fix was implemented and REVERTED. In isolation it looked
excellent (chan T3 3->22 rows; T2 0->108 cells; T9 0->14 cells; maier T8/T11
gained cells) but it broke 9 real-PDF tests across 4 files, because a real row
can legitimately be TALL: xiao Table 4's row 2 spans 94.4pt as a multi-line
stacked data block, and a hard anchor cap shatters it. The previous-word test
under-splits; a naive anchor cap over-splits. Neither rule alone is correct.

Ships the reproduction as xfail(strict) so the defect stays visible and a correct
fix XPASSes loudly, plus three plain-assert companions pinning behaviour that must
not regress while it is solved. FINDINGS doc records the measurements and three
candidate directions (re-merge on shared column occupancy; explicit chain-merge
signature detection; derive the row grid from the most stable column).

No library code changes — the tree is byte-identical to v2.4.120.

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): a table's own caption no longer condemns its own table (v2.4.120)
recent_commits.body:
RC-T cycle 4. _whitespace_grid_is_clean rejects any grid containing a
"Table N."/"Figure N." cell — the signature of a region that absorbed a
NEIGHBOURING table's caption. But _region_for_caption builds every region as
_union(caption_bbox, geom_bbox), so a caption-anchored region ALWAYS contains
its own caption by construction. The guard therefore condemned EVERY region
grid: whitespace_cells returned 0 cells corpus-wide (19/19 chan_feldman+maier
regions) and each table fell to the raw_text fallback, which truncates rows.
The guard's own comment said the marker proves the region absorbed "an adjacent
table's (or its own) caption" — the "or its own" clause was the bug.

The exemption is IDENTITY-based, not position-based: the anchoring caption's
number is threaded from the region spec / region.caption_match into the guard,
and a caption cell is exempt only when it names THAT exact number, sits in a
leading row, and is the first such match — per-CELL, and opt-in so the
auto-detect path keeps the strict legacy behaviour.

A position-only draft was written and REJECTED in cross-model review (codex);
all three of its holes reproduced locally: a neighbour's caption in a leading
row blessed as "own" (publishing another table's data), (r,c) sort order picking
the leftmost caption on side-by-side pages, and a whole-ROW exemption letting a
second Table/Figure caption ride along. Each is pinned by a regression test.

101-PDF guard-diff: 20 tables recover, 0 regressed, 0 foreign-caption
acceptances. Recovery spans ip_feldman, jdm_.2023.15, korbmacher, maier,
am_sociol_rev and socius — not just the papers that motivated the cycle.

Also in this commit (leave-nothing-behind):

* ReDoS in normalize._CI_UPPER_DROPPED_RE. The intermittently-red
  test_regex_no_catastrophic_backtracking was recorded as merely load-sensitive;
  unloaded it took 2.3-6.9s against a 5s budget. The driver is the decimal
  atom's UNBOUNDED integer part (\d*\.\d+), quadratic on a long digit run
  (~4.6x per doubling). Bounding it to \d{0,20} is ~270x faster with identical
  matching. The decoration-gap hypothesis was measured and REJECTED first.
  NORMALIZATION_VERSION deliberately not bumped: complexity only, no behaviour
  change.

* test_chan_feldman_table8_ci_upper_signs_recovered re-targeted. It read the
  2bi/2bii hypothesis rows out of Table 8 and passed only because the pairing
  was wrong. The AI gold confirms Table 8 is the intercorrelation matrix and
  Table 9 is "Summary of statistical tests" — cycle 4 FIXED that pairing. Now
  selects the hypothesis grid by content, not a hard-coded label; the
  substantive negative-CI assertions are unchanged and gold-exact.

chan_feldman is NOT fixed by this cycle and keeps its xfail(strict), with the
corrected diagnosis: its regions genuinely absorb 2-column body prose and fail
the prose/clean-data guards on their own merits (the separate region prose-trim
cycle). Its T5/T8 rejections are CORRECT — those regions really do reach into
Table 9's caption at grid row 4, the guard's original defence case, intact.

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): RC-T caption-tail walk — tables no longer drop their first rows (v2.4.119)
recent_commits.body:
The gated RC-T cycle (user-approved). `_extract_table_body_text`'s body_start
walk stepped break-to-break (preferring \n\n) with a 40-char window, so a
WRAPPED caption whose table body serializes column-by-column overshot the
caption's own terminator and SILENTLY DROPPED leading rows — chan_feldman
Table 3 lost its first four rows, Table 1 its first hypothesis row.

`_caption_tail_body_start` replaces it with a per-LINE walk carrying three
structural rules, each pinned by a corpus case the run-3 prototype regressed
on: whole-line terminator test (xiao T6), blank-line stop, and a max-wrap-lines
cap (amc_1 T3). Companion guards handle what the corrected walk now reaches:
`_skip_leading_nontable_junk` (leading figure caption / wrapped prose, bounded
+ terminated-only) and `_raw_text_is_page_furniture_only` (jama_open_1 T2
rendered ONLY a banner/title/date/"8/13"). `_line_is_body_prose` gains a
bibliography-row exemption.

Two corruptions the recovered rows EXPOSED (pre-existing, verified against a
v2.4.118 baseline — the data simply never reached the page before):
- S5b FFFD `>=` recovery was wired into channel 1 only, so plos_med Table 2's
  rows arrived as mojibake. Now wired into channel 3, with the document-
  consensus gate extended to count operators already present (unanimity kept).
- W0b-est: the estimate column is separated from its CI column by the SE
  column, so W0d's proximity window cannot span it (efendic T3 `21.34`).
  Estimates now pair with CIs POSITIONALLY, rewriting only when the corrected
  reading lands inside that CI and the literal one does not.

A recovery REJECTED before release: a `W0b-col` column-consensus rule flipped
efendic T5's `[2.42, 2.69]`, which the AI gold confirms is a GENUINELY POSITIVE
interval (Direction high-vs-low, est 2.56, p<.001) — it would have published a
sign-flipped effect. Removed; the case is pinned by a regression guard. The
pre-existing `_CORRUPT_CI_RE` was itself over-broad (matched ascending pairs,
asserting the wrong flip into existence) and is now descending-only. Standing
rule: a sign flip requires per-record evidence, never column membership.

Also: tests/conftest.py resolved fixtures under the dead ~/Dropbox/Vibe path,
so every articlerepo-keyed test SKIPPED silently (a green run that verified
nothing). Now VIBE_ROOT-aware.

Verification: 101-PDF guard-diff 333 captions recover / 0 truncations (the
prototype had 2); full suite 1872 passed (the one red is a load-sensitive
perf test that passes in isolation at 1.43s of a 5s budget); baseline 26/26;

told to check for it.

recent_commits.message: release(glyph): W0n p-threshold dropped-decimal recovery — v2.4.118
recent_commits.body:
ar_apa/JESP rendered `p < 05 (see Fig. 1)` — the significance threshold's
decimal point is drawn on the AdvGulliv broken-ToUnicode family and vanishes
from BOTH text channels (pdftotext emits nothing; the pdfplumber char stream
reads `p<05(see` with no dot char), so unlike W0h/W0m there is no layout
evidence to gate on. W0n `recover_p_threshold_dropped_decimal` is a pure

(05/01/001) after `<`/`>`/`≤`/`≥` is never legitimate notation. Four guards
(never `=`; canonical set only; no longer-number continuation;
significance-clause context) keep the 10-fold-wrong-number FP impossible on
the shapes the corpus actually contains (only other dotless sites corpus-wide
are legitimate `P = 1` exact values, excluded by the operator guard). Wired
channels 1+3; NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.45.

adversarial battery; real-PDF test fails at v2.4.117; full suite 1865 passed

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): RC-T caption-tail walk — tables no longer drop their first rows (v2.4.119)
recent_commits.body:
The gated RC-T cycle (user-approved). `_extract_table_body_text`'s body_start
walk stepped break-to-break (preferring \n\n) with a 40-char window, so a
WRAPPED caption whose table body serializes column-by-column overshot the
caption's own terminator and SILENTLY DROPPED leading rows — chan_feldman
Table 3 lost its first four rows, Table 1 its first hypothesis row.

`_caption_tail_body_start` replaces it with a per-LINE walk carrying three
structural rules, each pinned by a corpus case the run-3 prototype regressed
on: whole-line terminator test (xiao T6), blank-line stop, and a max-wrap-lines
cap (amc_1 T3). Companion guards handle what the corrected walk now reaches:
`_skip_leading_nontable_junk` (leading figure caption / wrapped prose, bounded
+ terminated-only) and `_raw_text_is_page_furniture_only` (jama_open_1 T2
rendered ONLY a banner/title/date/"8/13"). `_line_is_body_prose` gains a
bibliography-row exemption.

Two corruptions the recovered rows EXPOSED (pre-existing, verified against a
v2.4.118 baseline — the data simply never reached the page before):
- S5b FFFD `>=` recovery was wired into channel 1 only, so plos_med Table 2's
  rows arrived as mojibake. Now wired into channel 3, with the document-
  consensus gate extended to count operators already present (unanimity kept).
- W0b-est: the estimate column is separated from its CI column by the SE
  column, so W0d's proximity window cannot span it (efendic T3 `21.34`).
  Estimates now pair with CIs POSITIONALLY, rewriting only when the corrected
  reading lands inside that CI and the literal one does not.

A recovery REJECTED before release: a `W0b-col` column-consensus rule flipped
efendic T5's `[2.42, 2.69]`, which the AI gold confirms is a GENUINELY POSITIVE
interval (Direction high-vs-low, est 2.56, p<.001) — it would have published a
sign-flipped effect. Removed; the case is pinned by a regression guard. The
pre-existing `_CORRUPT_CI_RE` was itself over-broad (matched ascending pairs,
asserting the wrong flip into existence) and is now descending-only. Standing
rule: a sign flip requires per-record evidence, never column membership.

Also: tests/conftest.py resolved fixtures under the dead ~/Dropbox/Vibe path,
so every articlerepo-keyed test SKIPPED silently (a green run that verified
nothing). Now VIBE_ROOT-aware.

Verification: 101-PDF guard-diff 333 captions recover / 0 truncations (the
prototype had 2); full suite 1872 passed (the one red is a load-sensitive
perf test that passes in isolation at 1.43s of a 5s budget); baseline 26/26;
5-paper canary AI-verify — each fix independently confirmed by an auditor
told to check for it.

recent_commits.message: release(glyph): W0n p-threshold dropped-decimal recovery — v2.4.118
recent_commits.body:
ar_apa/JESP rendered `p < 05 (see Fig. 1)` — the significance threshold's
decimal point is drawn on the AdvGulliv broken-ToUnicode family and vanishes
from BOTH text channels (pdftotext emits nothing; the pdfplumber char stream
reads `p<05(see` with no dot char), so unlike W0h/W0m there is no layout
evidence to gate on. W0n `recover_p_threshold_dropped_decimal` is a pure
text-shape recovery: a dotless, leading-zero-free canonical threshold
(05/01/001) after `<`/`>`/`≤`/`≥` is never legitimate notation. Four guards
(never `=`; canonical set only; no longer-number continuation;
significance-clause context) keep the 10-fold-wrong-number FP impossible on
the shapes the corpus actually contains (only other dotless sites corpus-wide
are legitimate `P = 1` exact values, excluded by the operator guard). Wired
channels 1+3; NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.45.

Verification: 101-PDF raw-text FP scan CLEAN (target-only); 13-case
adversarial battery; real-PDF test fails at v2.4.117; full suite 1865 passed
(idempotency ratchet=0); 26-paper baseline 26/26; independent Sonnet audit
confirms `p < .05 (see Fig. 1)` matches gold with healthy thresholds
byte-identical.

Also in this release (leave-nothing-behind):
- tools/render_for_audit.py wrote CRLF while hashing LF — the recorded
  rendered_sha could never match the on-disk file (provenance footgun,
  surfaced live by the I10 artifact-existence gate). newline="\n" on both
  writes.
- tools/diag/{w0l_fp_scan,rct_body_text_diff}.py pointed at the dead
  pre-migration Dropbox corpus path — now resolve VIBE_ROOT and fail loudly
  instead of reporting a false CLEAN on 0 PDFs. New w0n_fp_scan.py harness.
- test_b1_whitespace_cells_wiring_live → xfail(strict) with the RC-T
  FINDINGS pointer (real TEXT-LOSS guard stays armed; suite exit honest).
- The two "(Camelot ON)" times-glyph tests now skip VISIBLY under
  DOCPLUCK_DISABLE_CAMELOT instead of false-failing/false-passing.

recent_commits.message: release(glyph): W0m β-as-'b' layout-gated recovery — v2.4.117 packaging
recent_commits.body:
Completes the v2.4.117 release for the W0m code that landed via 3b24a20 (the
Dropbox-damage restore commit recovered the uncommitted routine intact):
version bumps (__version__/pyproject 2.4.117; NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.44 was
in the restored file), CHANGELOG entry, tests, project lesson.

W0m recover_beta_via_layout: ar_apa (JESP 2009) drew the Greek β in the AdvPSMP
math-symbol font with no ToUnicode CMap, so pdftotext rendered all five
standardized coefficients as plain 'b' (`b = -.022` for `β = −.022`). A
text-only rewrite is unsafe ('b', unstandardized, is a legitimate distinct
statistic) — the layout font tag is the discriminator: a 'b' char in an
AdvPSMP-family font immediately before '=' is a corrupted β; flips at most as
many text slots as the layout counted (the W0h correlation mechanism).

Verification (ground truth = AI multimodal reading golds via article-finder):
- Independent Sonnet audit: all five ar_apa betas render β (4 signed correct;
  .245's minus stays the documented OCR-only limit). maier rotation audit:
  ZERO b→β false positives; H3a/H3b intact.
- 101-PDF layout FP scan: fires ONLY on the 2 JESP-2009 sibling papers
  (target + _010, 13 more betas recovered by the same font signature).
- Glyph+idempotency suite 97 passed; 26-paper baseline 26/26; 5 new unit tests

recent_commits.body:
Completes the v2.4.117 release for the W0m code that landed via 3b24a20 (the
Dropbox-damage restore commit recovered the uncommitted routine intact):
version bumps (__version__/pyproject 2.4.117; NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.44 was
in the restored file), CHANGELOG entry, tests, project lesson.

W0m recover_beta_via_layout: ar_apa (JESP 2009) drew the Greek β in the AdvPSMP
math-symbol font with no ToUnicode CMap, so pdftotext rendered all five
standardized coefficients as plain 'b' (`b = -.022` for `β = −.022`). A
text-only rewrite is unsafe ('b', unstandardized, is a legitimate distinct
statistic) — the layout font tag is the discriminator: a 'b' char in an
AdvPSMP-family font immediately before '=' is a corrupted β; flips at most as
many text slots as the layout counted (the W0h correlation mechanism).

Verification (ground truth = AI multimodal reading golds via article-finder):
- Independent Sonnet audit: all five ar_apa betas render β (4 signed correct;
  .245's minus stays the documented OCR-only limit). maier rotation audit:
  ZERO b→β false positives; H3a/H3b intact.
- 101-PDF layout FP scan: fires ONLY on the 2 JESP-2009 sibling papers
  (target + _010, 13 more betas recovered by the same font signature).
- Glyph+idempotency suite 97 passed; 26-paper baseline 26/26; 5 new unit tests
  + real-PDF render test asserting β (fails at v2.4.116).
- Also repaired the post-move broken editable install (pip -e at ~/Vibe).

recent_commits.message: fix(render): strip affiliation remnant orphaned in Abstract body (chandrashekar) + v2.4.115
recent_commits.body:
A canary AI-verify found chandrashekar_2023_mp rendering "Department of Philosophy,
Lake Forest College" + "*Joint first authors" right after the ## Abstract heading,
before the abstract prose. The paper has 3 author affiliations; the section
partitioner inserted ## Abstract mid-affiliation-block, so the masthead strip
(which stops AT ## Abstract) caught the first two but left the third orphaned in
the Abstract body, and the >=3-consecutive-line _strip_body_affiliation_block
could not reach a single surviving affiliation line.

Fix: _strip_abstract_zone_affiliation_remnant removes an affiliation line (+ a
joint-authors / corresponding-author companion note) that is the FIRST non-blank
content after ## Abstract. A real Abstract always opens with PROSE, so an
affiliation LINE in that slot is unambiguously a boundary-split front-matter
remnant -- the structural signature is affiliation-grammar (via the existing
_is_affiliation_line) at the Abstract-heading boundary, never paper identity. An
abstract that merely MENTIONS a university mid-sentence is prose, not an
affiliation line, and is kept.

Verification (AI-gold via article-finder): chandrashekar's ## Abstract now goes
directly to the abstract body; all 3 affiliations are in the front matter (stripped
by design), none in the Abstract. An abstract-zone FP-scan across the rendered
corpus fires ONLY on chandrashekar -- every other paper's abstract is byte-identical.
4 new tests (incl. real-abstract + university-mention FP guards). Full suite: 1896
passed, only the 2 documented pre-existing whitespace_cells failures remain.

Resolves chandrashekar's METADATA-LEAK (defect #1 of the 2026-07-04 report). Its
Tables 9/10 RC-T data-loss (defects #2/#3) is the architectural cluster --
diagnosed with a precise cycle plan in
docs/FINDINGS_2026-07-04_chandrashekar_rc_t_tables_9_10.md (the missing piece: wire
tables/whitespace.py::char_whitespace_cells to REPLACE a degenerate matched Camelot
table in extract_structured.py::_pick_better_table). Deferred to a dedicated gated
cycle (full 48-paper guard-diff + 7-canary AI-verify; do NOT rush at session-tail).

recent_commits.message: fix(glyph): recover 2 residual ×-as-3 prose shapes W0k can't reach (efendic) + v2.4.116
recent_commits.body:
W0l — the two ×-as-3 glyph residuals the single-line W0k word-pair regex
structurally cannot reach (both silently render `3` where a scientist should
read `×`), documented in docs/FINDINGS_2026-07-03_efendic_glyph_in_prose_channel.md:

(A) recover_times_design_notation — factorial-design notation `<digit>(…) 3
    <digit>(…)`: "2 (Between-subject factor--Direction: …) 3 2 (…) 3 3
    (Within-subject factor--…) mixed-subject design" → each `) 3 <digit> (`
    boundary's `3` is a corrupted `×` (trailing digit is the real factor SIZE).
    Fires ONLY when tied to a genuine factor parenthetical: an adjacent
    parenthetical names a factor type, OR both sides are factor-size parens
    closed by a factorial/design tail. A range recode `(min 1) 3 2 (max 5)`,
    a formula `f(x) 3 2 (y)`, `(from level 3) 3 2 (see note)` are left alone.

(B) recover_times_wrapped_interaction — a line ending `<Pred> 3` whose next
    line starts with a predictor word, inside an "interaction" context:
    "(Direction 3\nManipulated Attribute × CMA)" → "Direction × Manipulated…".
    Reference-word tail guard (FIGURE 3 / Table 3 / Model 3) — the wide FP
    scan caught amj_1 `FIGURE 3\nRegression…` + jamison `Table 3\nMain-effects
    and interactions.` wrongly joined; guard added + regression-tested.

NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.42 → 1.9.43. Wired channel 1 (normalize_text) AND
channel 3 (render post-process) per glyph-fixes-need-all-three-text-channels.

Verification (ground truth = AI multimodal reading golds via article-finder):
- Independent Sonnet canary audit CONFIRMS both efendic glyph fixes correct
  (design `× 2 × 3`, interaction `Direction × Manipulated Attribute × CMA`),
  no ×-as-3 / minus-as-2 corruption anywhere else in efendic.
- Wide 101-PDF raw-text FP scan CLEAN (0 non-target FPs; efendic recovered).
- 26-paper baseline 26/26 PASS. Normalize idempotency corpus PASS.
- 42 W0k/W0l tests + real-PDF end-to-end (fails at HEAD v2.4.115, passes here).

Resolves efendic's two ×-as-3 residuals. Remaining efendic findings (2 demoted
subsection headings; a NEW Table 4/5 mid-sentence splice) are queued; RC-T
table-data-loss on ip_feldman/plos_med/chandrashekar remains architectural.

recent_commits.message: fix(render): strip affiliation remnant orphaned in Abstract body (chandrashekar) + v2.4.115
recent_commits.body:
A canary AI-verify found chandrashekar_2023_mp rendering "Department of Philosophy,
Lake Forest College" + "*Joint first authors" right after the ## Abstract heading,
before the abstract prose. The paper has 3 author affiliations; the section
partitioner inserted ## Abstract mid-affiliation-block, so the masthead strip
(which stops AT ## Abstract) caught the first two but left the third orphaned in
the Abstract body, and the >=3-consecutive-line _strip_body_affiliation_block
could not reach a single surviving affiliation line.

Fix: _strip_abstract_zone_affiliation_remnant removes an affiliation line (+ a
joint-authors / corresponding-author companion note) that is the FIRST non-blank
content after ## Abstract. A real Abstract always opens with PROSE, so an
affiliation LINE in that slot is unambiguously a boundary-split front-matter
remnant -- the structural signature is affiliation-grammar (via the existing
_is_affiliation_line) at the Abstract-heading boundary, never paper identity. An
abstract that merely MENTIONS a university mid-sentence is prose, not an
affiliation line, and is kept.

Verification (AI-gold via article-finder): chandrashekar's ## Abstract now goes
directly to the abstract body; all 3 affiliations are in the front matter (stripped
by design), none in the Abstract. An abstract-zone FP-scan across the rendered
corpus fires ONLY on chandrashekar -- every other paper's abstract is byte-identical.
4 new tests (incl. real-abstract + university-mention FP guards). Full suite: 1896
passed, only the 2 documented pre-existing whitespace_cells failures remain.

Resolves chandrashekar's METADATA-LEAK (defect #1 of the 2026-07-04 report). Its
Tables 9/10 RC-T data-loss (defects #2/#3) is the architectural cluster --
diagnosed with a precise cycle plan in
docs/FINDINGS_2026-07-04_chandrashekar_rc_t_tables_9_10.md (the missing piece: wire
tables/whitespace.py::char_whitespace_cells to REPLACE a degenerate matched Camelot
table in extract_structured.py::_pick_better_table). Deferred to a dedicated gated
cycle (full 48-paper guard-diff + 7-canary AI-verify; do NOT rush at session-tail).
